units.zh: 邵續
units.en: Shao Xu
units.literal: Shao Xu

units.zh: 邵續，字嗣祖，魏郡安陽人也。
units.en: Shao Xu, courtesy Sizu, came from Anyang in Wei Commandery.
units.literal: Shao Xu, style name Sizu, was a man of Anyang in Wei Commandery.

units.zh: 父乘，散騎侍郎。
units.en: His father, Shao Cheng, had risen to gentleman attendant at leisure.
units.literal: His father Shao Cheng was gentleman attendant at leisure.

units.zh: 續樸素有志烈，博覽經史，善談理義，妙解天文。
units.en: Shao Xu lived plainly and held fierce convictions; he read deeply across the classics and histories, argued principle with ease, and read the stars with uncommon skill.
units.literal: Shao Xu was plain and frugal and possessed of fierce resolve; he read widely in the classics and histories, was skilled at discussing principle and meaning, and had a subtle grasp of astronomy.

units.zh: 初為成都王穎參軍，穎將討長沙王乂，續諫曰：「續聞兄弟如左右手，今明公當天下之敵，而欲去一手乎？
units.en: He first joined the staff of Prince Chengdu, Sima Ying. When Ying prepared to strike Prince Changsha, Sima Yi, Shao Xu urged him: "They say brothers are like a man's two hands; you stand against the whole realm—would you willingly cut one off?
units.literal: At first he served as army adviser to Prince Chengdu Sima Ying; when Ying was about to campaign against Prince Changsha Sima Yi, Shao Xu remonstrated: "I have heard that brothers are like the left and right hand; now the enlightened lord faces the empire's foes—would you wish to remove one hand?

units.zh: 續竊惑之。」
units.en: He could not fathom Ying's plan."
units.literal: Shao Xu privately was perplexed by this."

units.zh: 穎不納。
units.en: Ying would not listen.
units.literal: Ying did not accept it.

units.zh: 後為苟晞參軍，除沁水令。
units.en: He later served on Gou Xi's staff and was named magistrate of Qinshui.
units.literal: Later he served as army adviser to Gou Xi and was appointed magistrate of Qinshui.

units.zh: 時天下漸亂，續去縣還家，糾合亡命，得數百人。
units.en: As the empire slid toward chaos, Shao Xu quit his post, went home, and gathered several hundred outlaws around him.
units.literal: At that time the realm was gradually falling into chaos; Shao Xu left the county and returned home, rallied fugitives from the law, and obtained several hundred men.

units.zh: 王浚假續綏集將軍、樂陵太守，屯厭次，以續子乂為督護。
units.en: Wang Jun named him acting General Who Pacifies and Gathers and prefect of Leling, stationed him at Yanci, and put his son Shao Yi in charge as chief of staff.
units.literal: Wang Jun provisionally appointed Shao Xu General Who Pacifies and Gathers and prefect of Leling, garrisoned Yanci, and appointed Shao Xu's son Shao Yi as chief of staff.

units.zh: 續綏懷流散，多歸附之。
units.en: He sheltered displaced people, and a great many rallied to his banner.
units.literal: Shao Xu comforted and gathered scattered refugees, and many attached themselves to him.

units.zh: 石勒既破浚，遣乂還招續，續以孤危無援，權附於勒，勒亦以乂為督護。
units.en: When Shi Le had broken Wang Jun, he sent Shao Yi back to win his father over; isolated and without allies, Shao Xu submitted for the moment to Shi Le, who again named Shao Yi chief of staff.
units.literal: After Shi Le had defeated Wang Jun, he sent Shao Yi back to summon Shao Xu; Shao Xu, isolated and without aid, submitted provisionally to Shi Le, and Shi Le likewise appointed Shao Yi chief of staff.

units.zh: 既而段匹磾在薊，遺書要續俱歸元帝，續從之。
units.en: Before long Duan Pidi, holding Ji, wrote urging Shao Xu to come south with him to Emperor Yuan, and Shao Xu agreed.
units.literal: Not long after, Duan Pidi was at Ji; he sent a letter inviting Shao Xu to return together to Emperor Yuan, and Shao Xu followed him.

units.zh: 其下諫曰：「今棄勒歸匹磾，任子危矣。」
units.en: His officers warned him: "Turn from Shi Le to Duan Pidi and the son you left as hostage is lost."
units.literal: His subordinates remonstrated: "If we now abandon Shi Le for Duan Pidi, the hostage son will be in peril."

units.zh: 續垂泣曰：「我出身為國，豈得顧子而為叛臣哉！」
units.en: Shao Xu wept and said, "I entered public life for the dynasty—am I to save my boy and turn traitor?"
units.literal: Shao Xu wept and said: "I left home to serve the state—how could I care for my son and become a traitor!"

units.zh: 遂絕於勒，勒乃害乂。
units.en: He broke with Shi Le; Shi Le then executed Shao Yi.
units.literal: Thereupon he broke with Shi Le, whereupon Shi Le had Shao Yi killed.

units.zh: 續懼勒攻，先求救於匹磾，匹磾遣弟文鴦救續。
units.en: Fearing Shi Le's assault, he appealed first to Duan Pidi, who sent his brother Wenyang to his rescue.
units.literal: Shao Xu feared an attack by Shi Le and first begged help from Duan Pidi; Pidi sent his younger brother Duan Wenyang to relieve Shao Xu.

units.zh: 文鴦未至，勒已率八千騎圍續。
units.en: Shi Le reached him first with eight thousand cavalry and threw a ring around his position.
units.literal: Before Wenyang had arrived, Shi Le had already led eight thousand horsemen to besiege Shao Xu.

units.zh: 勒素畏鮮卑，又聞文鴦至，乃棄攻具東走。
units.en: Shi Le had always dreaded the Xianbei; at word of Wenyang's approach he abandoned his engines and bolted east.
units.literal: Shi Le had always feared the Xianbei, and when he heard Wenyang was coming he abandoned his siege equipment and fled east.

units.zh: 續與文鴦追勒至安陵，不及，虜勒所署官，並驅三千餘家，又遣騎入抄勒北邊，掠常山，亦二千家而還。
units.en: Shao Xu and Wenyang chased him to Anling but could not catch him; they took the officials Shi Le had installed, marched off over three thousand families, sent riders to scour his northern marches and sack Changshan, and came back with two thousand more households besides.
units.literal: Shao Xu and Wenyang pursued Shi Le to Anling but did not overtake him; they captured Shi Le's appointed officials, drove off more than three thousand households, also sent cavalry to raid Shi Le's northern border, plundered Changshan, and likewise returned with two thousand households.

units.zh: 匹磾既殺劉琨，夷晉多怨叛，遂率其徒依續。
units.en: Once Duan Pidi had murdered Liu Kun, many Chinese and tribal followers turned against him, so he brought his host to Shao Xu's side.
units.literal: After Duan Pidi had killed Liu Kun, Chinese and tribesmen for the most part resented him and rebelled; he therefore led his followers to rely on Shao Xu.

units.zh: 勒南和令趙領等率廣川、渤海千餘家背勒歸續。
units.en: Zhao Ling of Nanhe, serving under Shi Le, led over a thousand families from Guangchuan and Bohai to defect to Shao Xu.
units.literal: Zhao Ling, magistrate of Nanhe under Shi Le, led more than a thousand households from Guangchuan and Bohai to betray Shi Le and join Shao Xu.

units.zh: 而帝以續為平原樂安太守、右將軍、冀州刺史，進平北將軍、假節，封祝阿子。
units.en: The court named him prefect of Pingyuan and Le'an, General of the Right, and inspector of Ji, then promoted him to General Who Pacifies the North with baton of authority and created him viscount of Zhu'e.
units.literal: The emperor appointed Shao Xu prefect of Pingyuan and Le'an, General of the Right, and inspector of Ji province, advanced him to General Who Pacifies the North with credential, and enfeoffed him as viscount of Zhu'e.

units.zh: 續遣兄子武邑內史存與文鴦率匹磾眾就食平原，為石季龍所破。
units.en: He dispatched his nephew Cun, Wuyi's interior governor, with Wenyang to escort Pidi's people into Pingyuan for supplies; Shi Hu shattered their force.
units.literal: Shao Xu sent his nephew Cun, interior governor of Wuyi, and Wenyang to lead Pidi's followers to forage in Pingyuan; they were defeated by Shi Jilong.

units.zh: 續先與曹嶷互相侵掠，嶷因存等敗，乃破續屯田，又抄其戶口，續首尾相救，疲於奔命。
units.en: Shao Xu and Cao Yi had long raided one another; after Cun's defeat Yi overran his military farms and seized his people, leaving Shao Xu racing from front to rear until he was worn threadbare.
units.literal: Shao Xu had earlier raided back and forth with Cao Yi; Yi because Cun and the others were defeated then smashed Shao Xu's military colonies and plundered his registered households; Shao Xu rescued head and tail in turn and was exhausted running from crisis to crisis.

units.zh: 太興初，續遣存及文鴦屯濟南黃巾固，因以逼嶷，嶷懼，求和。
units.en: Early in the Taixing era he sent Cun and Wenyang to hold the old Yellow Turban stronghold at Jinan and squeeze Cao Yi until Yi sued for peace.
units.literal: At the beginning of Taixing, Shao Xu sent Cun and Wenyang to garrison the Yellow Turban fort at Jinan in order to pressure Cao Yi; Yi feared and sued for peace.

units.zh: 俄而匹磾率眾攻段末杯，石勒知續孤危，遣季龍乘虛圍續。
units.en: Then Pidi marched against Duan Mobo; Shi Le, seeing Shao Xu left exposed, sent Shi Hu to fall on him while his guard was down.
units.literal: Soon Pidi led his host to attack Duan Mobo; Shi Le, knowing Shao Xu was isolated and imperiled, sent Shi Jilong to exploit the void and besiege Shao Xu.

units.zh: 季龍騎至城下，掠其居人，續率眾出救，季龍伏騎斷其後，遂為季龍所得，使續降其城。
units.en: Shi Hu rode to the walls and dragged off the townsfolk; Shao Xu sortied to save them, but Hu's hidden horse cut his retreat and took him prisoner, then ordered him to talk the garrison down.
units.literal: Shi Jilong's cavalry reached the foot of the city, plundered its inhabitants; Shao Xu led his host out to rescue them; Shi Jilong ambushed cavalry and cut off his rear; thereupon he was taken by Shi Jilong; he had Shao Xu persuade the city to surrender.

units.zh: 續呼其兄子竺等曰：「吾志雪國難，以報所受，不幸至此。
units.en: He called his nephews Zhu and the rest: "I meant to clear the throne's disgrace and repay every favor the court showed me; fate has brought me here instead.
units.literal: Shao Xu called to his elder brother's sons Zhu and the others: "My will was to wipe away the state's shame and repay what I received; unluckily I have reached this point.

units.zh: 汝等努力自勉，便奉匹磾為主，勿有二心。」
units.en: Bear up, every one of you, take Duan Pidi as your chief, and never divide your loyalty."
units.literal: You must strive with all your strength, then acknowledge Pidi as lord—do not harbor a second heart."

units.zh: 時帝既聞續沒，下詔曰：「邵續忠烈在公，義誠慷慨，綏集荒餘，憂國亡身。
units.en: Learning of Shao Xu's fall, the emperor promulgated an edict: "Shao Xu served the realm with blazing loyalty; his sense of duty ran high; he gathered the broken remnants of the north and gave his life for the dynasty.
units.literal: When the emperor had heard that Shao Xu was lost, he issued an edict: "Shao Xu's loyalty and fierce integrity were for the public good; in righteousness he was fervent; he gathered the scattered survivors of the wilderness and gave his body for the state.

units.zh: 功勳未遂，不幸陷沒，朕用悼恨於懷。
units.en: His work was unfinished when disaster swallowed him; I carry sorrow and regret in my breast.
units.literal: Merit and enterprise were not yet completed when he was engulfed in disaster; I therefore harbor grief and regret in my heart.

units.zh: 所統任重，宜時有代。
units.en: The post he held was too grave to stand empty; a successor must be named at once.
units.literal: The command he bore was weighty and should at this time have a successor.

units.zh: 其部曲文武，已共推其息緝為營主。
units.en: His staff and troops have together raised his son Ji to lead the camp.
units.literal: The civil and military officers of his army corps have jointly recommended his son Ji as camp commander.

units.zh: 續之忠誠，著於公私，今立其子，足以安眾，一以續本位即授緝，使總率所統，效節國難，雪其家仇。」
units.en: His faithfulness shone at court and in the ranks alike; naming his heir will steady the army—invest Ji with every title his father held, let him lead the old command, serve the throne through this ordeal, and wipe away the family's blood-debt."
units.literal: Shao Xu's loyalty has been manifest in public and private alike; now that we establish his son, it should be enough to reassure the host—in one act grant him Shao Xu's former rank and invest Ji, that he may command all who followed his father, devote his strength to the state's crisis, and avenge his family's wrongs."

units.zh: 季龍遣使送續於勒，勒使使徐光讓之曰：「國家應符撥亂，八表宅心，遺晉怖威，遠竄揚越。
units.en: Shi Hu sent Shao Xu to Shi Le, who had Xu Guang rebuke him: "Our house holds the mandate and stills turmoil; the world turns to us; the rump Jin tremble and scatter toward the Yangzi and the south.
units.literal: Shi Jilong sent Shao Xu under escort to Shi Le; Shi Le ordered his envoy Xu Guang to reproach him: "The state bears the tally and quells chaos; the eight quarters nestle at our heart; the remnant Jin fear our might and flee far to Yang and Yue.

units.zh: 而續蟻封海阿，跋扈王命，以夷狄不足為君邪？
units.en: Yet you crouch like ants on a coastal hillock and flout the Son of Heaven—do you imagine that we barbarians are unfit to rule?
units.literal: Yet you, Shao Xu, are like ants sealing a mound beside the sea, arrogant toward the king's command—do you hold that barbarians are unworthy to be lords?

units.zh: 何無上之甚也！
units.en: Never have I seen such contempt for authority!
units.literal: How extreme is your lack of respect for what is above!

units.zh: 國有常刑，于分甘乎？」
units.en: The law has its fixed penalties; will you go to your fate willingly?"
units.literal: The state has its constant punishments—as for the lot assigned you, are you content with it?"

units.zh: 續對曰：「晉末饑亂，奔控無所，保合鄉宗，庶全老幼。
units.en: Shao Xu answered: "When the Jin collapsed in famine and riot there was nowhere to run; I drew my clansmen together only to keep the old and the young alive.
units.literal: Shao Xu replied: "In the Jin's final years there was famine and chaos; there was nowhere to flee; I banded with my townspeople hoping to preserve the old and young in full.

units.zh: 屬大王龍飛之始，委命納質，精誠無感，不蒙慈恕。
units.en: At your first rising I offered my life and sent hostages; my good faith never moved you, and I was shown no mercy.
units.literal: When the Great King first rose like a dragon I placed my life in your hands and sent hostages; my earnest devotion aroused no response—I was not favored with merciful forgiveness.

units.zh: 言歸遺晉，仍荷寵授，誓盡忠節，實無二心。
units.en: When I went back to the Jin they heaped rank on me; I swore the fullest loyalty and never wavered inwardly.
units.literal: When I returned to the remnant Jin I still received thick honors; I swore to exhaust loyalty to the utmost—I truly had no second heart.

units.zh: 且受彼厚榮，而復二三其趣者，恐亦不容于明朝矣。
units.en: Besides, a man who took their lavish favors and then tacked with every wind would find no room even in a clear-sighted court.
units.literal: Moreover, one who took such thick honors from them and then shifted his purpose this way and that would hardly be tolerated by a luminous court either.

units.zh: 周文生於東夷，大禹出於西羌，帝王之興，蓋惟天命所屬，德之所招，當何常邪！
units.en: King Wen sprang from the eastern Yi, Great Yu from the western Qiang—dynasties rise where Heaven places them and virtue calls; what single rule could bind them?
units.literal: King Wen of the Zhou was born among the Eastern Yi; the Great Yu came from the Western Qiang—the rise of emperors and kings is surely whatever Heaven assigns and virtue summons; how can there be one constant rule!

units.zh: 伏惟大王聖武自天，道隆虞夏，凡在含生，孰不延首神化，恥隔皇風，而況囚乎！
units.en: I dare say your sacred might is heaven-sent and your virtue outshines Yu and Xia—every living soul longs for your transforming rule and is ashamed to stand outside your breeze—how much more a prisoner in your hands!
units.literal: Humbly I reflect: the Great King's sacred martial prowess comes from Heaven; his way towers above Yu and Xia—among everything that draws breath, who would not crane toward divine transformation and blush to be shut off from your royal airs—how much more a captive like myself!

units.zh: 使囚去真即偽，不得早叩天門者，大王負囚，囚不負大王也。
units.en: Should you force me from truth into treachery and bar me from serving the rightful court, the fault will be yours, Great King, not mine.
units.literal: If you make me leave the true for the false and keep me from knocking early at Heaven's gate, the Great King will have wronged this captive—this captive will not have wronged the Great King.

units.zh: 釁鼓之刑，囚之恆分，但恨天實為之，謂之何哉！」
units.en: Death on the drum is what any prisoner expects; I only grieve that Heaven willed it so—what more is there to say?"
units.literal: The punishment of smearing blood on the war drum is the captive's constant lot; I only regret that Heaven brought it about—what can one say!"

units.zh: 勒曰：「其言慨至，孤愧之多矣。
units.en: Shi Le said, "He speaks from the depths; I am ashamed before him.
units.literal: Shi Le said: "His words are fervent to the utmost; I am much ashamed before him.

units.zh: 夫忠於其君者，乃吾所求也。」
units.en: A man loyal to his sovereign is the very thing I prize."
units.literal: One who is loyal to his lord is exactly what I seek."

units.zh: 命張寶延之於館，厚撫之，尋以為從事中郎。
units.en: He told Zhang Bao to lodge him with honor, showered him with gifts, and soon named him palace retainer.
units.literal: He ordered Zhang Bao to extend him in a guest house, treated him generously, and soon appointed him retainer clerk.

units.zh: 今自後諸克敵擒俊，皆送之，不得輒害，冀獲如續之流。
units.en: Henceforth every time you break an enemy and seize a noted leader, bring him here alive—never kill such men on your own; I want more captives with Shao Xu's mettle.
units.literal: From now on whenever you crush the foe and seize outstanding captives, send them here alive—do not kill them at will; I hope to obtain more men in Shao Xu's mold.

units.zh: 初，季龍之攻續也，朝廷有王敦之逼，不遑救恤。
units.en: While Shi Hu besieged Shao Xu, the court was pinned by Wang Dun and could spare no rescue.
units.literal: Earlier, when Shi Jilong had attacked Shao Xu, the court was pressed by Wang Dun and had no leisure to send relief.

units.zh: 續既為勒所執，身灌園鬻菜，以供衣食。
units.en: Once in Shi Le's hands he tended gardens and peddled greens with his own hands to earn his keep.
units.literal: After Shao Xu was taken by Shi Le, he personally watered gardens and sold vegetables to supply clothing and food.

units.zh: 勒屢遣察之，歎曰；
units.en: Shi Le sent watchers again and again, then sighed and said:
units.literal: Shi Le repeatedly sent men to observe him and sighed, saying:

units.zh: 「此真高人矣。
units.en: "Here is a man who stands apart from the crowd.
units.literal: "This is truly a man set above the common run.

units.zh: 不如是，安足貴乎！」
units.en: Were it otherwise he would not be worth honoring at all!"
units.literal: Were it not so, how would he be worthy of esteem!"

units.zh: 嘉其清苦，數賜穀帛。
units.en: He admired his austerity and sent grain and cloth time after time.
units.literal: He praised his austerity and several times bestowed grain and silk.

units.zh: 每臨朝嗟歎，以勵群官。
units.en: At every audience he praised Shao Xu aloud to steel his ministers.
units.literal: Whenever he faced court he sighed with praise to encourage the host of officials.

units.zh: 續被獲之後，存及竺、緝等與匹磾嬰城距寇，而帝又假存揚武將軍、武邑太守。
units.en: After Shao Xu fell, Cun, Zhu, Ji, and the rest held the walls with Duan Pidi against the foe while the court named Cun General Who Rouses Valor and prefect of Wuyi.
units.literal: After Shao Xu was captured, Cun along with Zhu, Ji, and the others, with Pidi, sealed the city against the invaders; the emperor concurrently appointed Cun General Who Rouses Valor and prefect of Wuyi.

units.zh: 勒屢遣季龍攻之，戰守疲苦，不能自立。
units.en: Shi Le hurled Shi Hu against them again and again until attack and defense alike broke their strength.
units.literal: Shi Le repeatedly sent Shi Jilong to attack them; battle and defense wore them down until they could not establish themselves.

units.zh: 久之，匹磾及其弟文鴦與竺、緝等悉見獲，惟存得潰圍南奔，在道為賊所殺。
units.en: In time Pidi, Wenyang, Zhu, and Ji were all taken; only Cun burst the ring and ran south, only to die at bandit hands on the road.
units.literal: After a long time Pidi and his younger brother Wenyang with Zhu, Ji, and the others were all captured; only Cun broke out of the encirclement and fled south, but on the road was killed by bandits.

units.zh: 續竟亦遇害。
units.en: Shao Xu too was put to death in the end.
units.literal: Shao Xu in the end was likewise killed.

units.zh: 李矩
units.en: Li Ju
units.literal: Li Ju

units.zh: 李矩，字世回，平陽人也。
units.en: Li Ju, courtesy Shihui, came from Pingyang.
units.literal: Li Ju, style name Shihui, was a man of Pingyang.

units.zh: 童齔時，與群兒聚戲，便為其率，計畫指授，有成人之量。
units.en: Even as a boy, when he played with neighborhood children he always commanded them, laying plans like a grown man.
units.literal: In childhood when he gathered with other children to play, he became their leader, planning and directing as would an adult.

units.zh: 及長，為吏，送故縣令于長安，征西將軍梁王肜以為牙門。
units.en: As a young man he served as a clerk; escorting a former magistrate to Chang'an, he was recruited as a gate guard by Sima Rong, Prince of Liang, the general commanding the western expedition.
units.literal: When grown he became a clerk; seeing off a former magistrate to Chang'an, the western expedition general Sima Rong, Prince of Liang, took him on as yamen guard.

units.zh: 伐氐齊萬年有殊功，封東明亭侯。
units.en: He won outstanding distinction against the Di rebel Qi Wannian and was created village marquis of Dongming.
units.literal: In the campaign against the Di rebel Qi Wannian he had exceptional merit and was enfeoffed as village marquis of Dongming.

units.zh: 還為本郡督護。
units.en: Back home he became chief of staff of his commandery.
units.literal: On his return he was chief of staff for his native commandery.

units.zh: 太守宋胄欲以所親吳畿代之，矩謝病去。
units.en: Prefect Song Zhou meant to swap him for a favorite, Wu Ji; Li Ju pleaded illness and stepped down.
units.literal: The prefect Song Zhou wished to replace him with his intimate Wu Ji; Li Ju pleaded illness and departed.

units.zh: 畿恐矩復還，陰使人刺矩，會有人救之，故得免。
units.en: Wu Ji dreaded his return and hired an assassin; a passerby saved him and he lived.
units.literal: Wu Ji feared Li Ju might return and secretly sent someone to stab Li Ju; someone rescued him, therefore he escaped.

units.zh: 屬劉元海攻平陽，百姓奔走，矩素為鄉人所愛，乃推為塢主，東屯滎陽，後移新鄭。
units.en: When Liu Yuan stormed Pingyang and the people scattered, the locals, who loved Li Ju, made him chief of their fort; he moved east to Xingyang and later shifted to Xinzheng.
units.literal: When Liu Yuan attacked Pingyang and the common people fled in panic, Li Ju was loved by his townspeople and was pushed to be fortress chief; he encamped east at Xingyang and later moved to Xinzheng.

units.zh: 矩勇毅多權略，志在立功，東海王越以為汝陰太守。
units.en: Bold, resolute, and full of schemes, he burned to make his mark; Prince Donghai, Sima Yue, named him prefect of Ruyin.
units.literal: Li Ju was brave and resolute and full of stratagems; his aim was set on achievement; Prince Donghai Sima Yue appointed him prefect of Ruyin.

units.zh: 永嘉初，使矩與汝南太守袁孚率眾修洛陽千金堨，以利運漕。
units.en: Early in the Yongjia reign he and Yuan Fu, prefect of Runan, were ordered to restore Luoyang's Qianjin weir for the grain boats.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yongjia the court had Li Ju and the prefect of Runan, Yuan Fu, lead their forces to repair the Qianjin weir at Luoyang to benefit transport by canal.

units.zh: 及洛陽不守，太尉荀籓奔陽城，衛將軍華薈奔成皋。
units.en: When Luoyang fell, grand commandant Xun Fan ran to Yangcheng and guard general Hua Hui to Chenggao.
units.literal: When Luoyang did not hold, grand commandant Xun Fan fled to Yangcheng and guard general Hua Hui fled to Chenggao.

units.zh: 時大饑，賊帥侯都等每略人而食之，籓、薈部曲多為所啖。
units.en: Famine stalked the land; the outlaw Hou Du and his gang seized people for food, and many of Xun Fan's and Hua Hui's followers were eaten.
units.literal: At that time there was great famine; the bandit chieftain Hou Du and others repeatedly seized people and ate them; many of Fan's and Hui's retainers were devoured.

units.zh: 矩討都等滅之，乃營護籓、薈，各為立屋宇，輸穀以給之。
units.en: Li Ju destroyed Hou Du, then sheltered Fan and Hui, building houses for both and sending grain to keep them fed.
units.literal: Li Ju campaigned against Hou Du and destroyed them, then protected Fan and Hui, for each building houses and shipping grain to supply them.

units.zh: 及籓承制，建行臺，假矩滎陽太守。
units.en: When Xun Fan took acting authority and raised a field headquarters, he named Li Ju provisional prefect of Xingyang.
units.literal: When Fan assumed plenipotentiary command and set up a mobile headquarters, he provisionally named Li Ju prefect of Xingyang.

units.zh: 矩招懷離散，遠近多附之。
units.en: He called in the displaced and won over people from every quarter.
units.literal: Li Ju summoned and comforted the scattered; near and far largely attached themselves to him.

units.zh: 石勒親率大眾襲矩，矩遣老弱入山，令所在散牛馬，因設伏以待之。
units.en: Shi Le marched in person against him; Li Ju sent the noncombatants into the hills, turned cattle and horses loose across the countryside, and laid a trap.
units.literal: Shi Le personally led a great host against Li Ju; Li Ju sent the old and weak into the mountains and had people everywhere loose oxen and horses, then set an ambush to await him.

units.zh: 賊爭取牛馬。
units.en: Shi Le's men scrambled to round up the livestock.
units.literal: The bandits vied to seize the oxen and horses.

units.zh: 伏發，齊呼，聲動山谷，遂大破之，斬獲甚眾，勒乃退。
units.en: The ambush sprang; a single roar shook the valleys; Li Ju shattered the army with heavy slaughter and drove Shi Le back.
units.literal: The ambush rose; they shouted in unison; the sound shook the valleys; thereupon they greatly defeated him, killing and capturing very many, and Shi Le withdrew.

units.zh: 籓表元帝，加矩冠軍將軍，軺車幢蓋，進封陽武縣侯，領河東、平陽太守。
units.en: Xun Fan recommended him to Emperor Yuan, who added General Who Crowns the Army, a light chariot with canopy, raised his fief to county marquis of Yangwu, and let him serve jointly as prefect of Hedong and Pingyang.
units.literal: Xun Fan presented Li Ju to Emperor Yuan, who added to Li Ju the titles General Who Crowns the Army, light chariot with canopy, advanced his fief to county marquis of Yangwu, and had him hold the offices of prefect of Hedong and Pingyang.

units.zh: 時饑饉相仍，又多疫癘，矩垂心撫恤，百姓賴焉。
units.en: Famine and plague ran together; Li Ju poured his energy into relief, and the people clung to him.
units.literal: At that time famine followed famine and pestilence spread; Li Ju lavished care on relief and comfort, and the people relied on him.

units.zh: 會長安群盜東下，所在多虜掠，矩遣部將擊破之，盡得賊所略婦女千餘人。
units.en: When eastern raiders from Chang'an swept through the region, he sent a deputy to crush them and recovered over a thousand women they had taken.
units.literal: It happened that bandits from Chang'an moved east, plundering wherever they went; Li Ju sent a subordinate general to break them and fully obtained the more than a thousand women the bandits had seized.

units.zh: 諸將以非矩所部。
units.en: His officers argued that these captives were not from his own command.
units.literal: The generals held that they were not under Li Ju's command.

units.zh: 欲遂留之。
units.en: They wanted to keep the women for themselves.
units.literal: They wished to detain them.

units.zh: 矩曰：「俱是國家臣妾，焉有此彼此！」
units.en: Li Ju said, "They are all the emperor's people—how can we draw a line between his household and mine?"
units.literal: Li Ju said: "They are all alike subjects of the state—how can there be this distinction of yours and mine!"

units.zh: 乃一時遣之。
units.en: He sent every one of them home together.
units.literal: Thereupon he sent them off all at once.

units.zh: 時劉琨所假河內太守郭默為劉元海所逼，乞歸於矩，矩將使其甥郭誦迎致之，而不敢進。
units.en: Guo Mo, Liu Kun's acting prefect of Henei, was harried by Liu Yuan and begged Li Ju for refuge; Li Ju meant to send his nephew Guo Song to escort him in, but Song hesitated to move.
units.literal: At that time Guo Mo, whom Liu Kun had provisionally appointed prefect of Henei, was pressed by Liu Yuan and begged to return to Li Ju; Li Ju was about to have his nephew Guo Song go welcome him but did not dare advance.

units.zh: 會劉琨遣參軍張肇，率鮮卑範勝等五百餘騎往長安，屬默被圍，道路不通，將還依邵續，行至矩營，矩謂肇曰：「默是劉公所授，公家之事，知無不為。」
units.en: Just then Liu Kun dispatched Zhang Zhao with over five hundred Xianbei horse under Fan Sheng toward Chang'an; blocked by the siege of Guo Mo, they turned back toward Shao Xu and halted at Li Ju's camp. Li Ju told Zhang Zhao, "Guo Mo holds Liu Kun's commission; whatever serves your patron's interest, I will do."
units.literal: It happened that Liu Kun sent adjutant Zhang Zhao leading more than five hundred Xianbei riders under Fan Sheng and others toward Chang'an; because Guo Mo was besieged the roads were not open; they were about to return and rely on Shao Xu; when they reached Li Ju's camp, Li Ju said to Zhang Zhao: "Guo Mo was appointed by Lord Liu; in matters of your master's house, I know there is nothing I would not do.

units.zh: 屠各舊畏鮮卑，遂邀肇為聲援，肇許之。
units.en: The Tuge had always dreaded Xianbei horse, so Li Ju asked Zhang Zhao to lend their visible support; Zhao agreed.
units.literal: The Tuge had long feared the Xianbei; Li Ju therefore invited Zhang Zhao to lend visible support, and Zhao consented.

units.zh: 賊望見鮮卑，不戰而走。
units.en: The besiegers sighted the Xianbei and bolted without offering battle.
units.literal: The bandits, seeing the Xianbei, fled without fighting.

units.zh: 誦潛遣輕舟濟河，使勇士夜襲懷城，掩賊留營，又大破之。
units.en: Guo Song slipped light boats across the river and sent picked men to storm Huai by night, falling on the enemy rear camp and routing them again.
units.literal: Guo Song secretly sent light boats across the Yellow River and bold men to raid Huai city by night, surprise the bandit camp left behind, and again greatly defeated them.

units.zh: 默遂率其屬歸於矩。
units.en: Guo Mo then brought his command to Li Ju.
units.literal: Guo Mo thereupon led his following to submit to Li Ju.

units.zh: 後劉聰遣從弟暢步騎三萬討矩，屯于韓王故壘，相去七里，遣使招矩。
units.en: Later Liu Cong dispatched his cousin Liu Chang with thirty thousand foot and horse against Li Ju, pitching camp on Han Wang's old fort seven li off, and sent a herald to call Li Ju in.
units.literal: Later Liu Cong sent his cousin Liu Chang with thirty thousand foot and horse to campaign against Li Ju, encamping at the old rampart of Han Wang seven li away, and sent a messenger to summon Li Ju.

units.zh: 時暢卒至，矩未暇為備，遣使奉牛酒詐降於暢，潛匿精勇，見其老弱。
units.en: Liu Chang came on too fast for Li Ju to ready a defense, so he sent oxen and wine as a sham surrender while hiding his veterans and parading only the aged and feeble.
units.literal: At that time Liu Chang had arrived suddenly; Li Ju had no time to prepare; he sent envoys bearing oxen and wine feigning surrender to Liu Chang while hiding picked warriors and showing him only the old and weak.

units.zh: 暢不以為虞，大饗渠帥，人皆醉飽。
units.en: Liu Chang dropped his guard, threw a great feast for his chiefs, and they all drank themselves full.
units.literal: Liu Chang took no precautions, feasted his chieftains grandly, and everyone was drunk and full.

units.zh: 矩謀夜襲之，兵士以賊眾，皆有懼色。
units.en: Li Ju meant to strike by night, but his men blanched at the size of the enemy host.
units.literal: Li Ju planned a night raid; his soldiers, seeing the enemy's numbers, all showed fear on their faces.

units.zh: 矩令郭誦禱鄭子產祠曰：「君昔相鄭，惡鳥不鳴。
units.en: He told Guo Song to pray at Zichan of Zheng's temple: "When you ruled Zheng, ill-omened birds fell silent.
units.literal: Li Ju ordered Guo Song to pray at the shrine of Zichan of Zheng: "You once served Zheng as minister—even ill-omened birds did not cry.

units.zh: 凶胡臭羯，何得過庭！」
units.en: What business have murderous Hu and reeking Jie in this court!"
units.literal: How can foul barbarians and stinking Jie cross this courtyard!"

units.zh: 使巫揚言：「東裏有教，當遣神兵相助。」
units.en: He set shamans to cry abroad: "The eastern god has spoken—heaven will send warriors to our aid."
units.literal: He had shamans proclaim loudly: "The god of the eastern quarter has issued a command—divine soldiers are to be sent to aid us."

units.zh: 將士聞之，皆踴躍爭進。
units.en: The troops heard it and surged forward, each man eager to be first.
units.literal: When officers and men heard this, all leaped up vying to advance.

units.zh: 乃使誦及督護楊璋等選勇敢千人，夜掩暢營，獲鎧馬甚多，斬首數千級，暢僅以身免。
units.en: He sent Guo Song with Yang Zhang and other picked men—one thousand bold fighters—to fall on Chang's camp at night. They took stacks of armored horses, heaped up thousands of heads, and Chang alone slipped away alive.
units.literal: He then had Guo Song and chief of staff Yang Zhang and others pick a thousand brave men and strike Liu Chang's camp by night; they seized very many armored horses and cut off several thousand heads; Chang barely escaped with his life.

units.zh: 先是，郭默聞矩被攻，遣弟芝率眾援之。
units.en: Before this, Guo Mo had learned that Li Ju was pressed and dispatched his brother Zhi with troops to help.
units.literal: Earlier, when Guo Mo heard Li Ju was under attack, he sent his younger brother Zhi with a host to aid him.

units.zh: 既而聞破暢，芝復馳來赴矩。
units.en: When word came that Chang was broken, Zhi raced back to Li Ju's side.
units.literal: Afterward, hearing Chang had been defeated, Zhi again galloped to join Li Ju.

units.zh: 矩乃與芝馬五百匹，分軍為三道，夜追賊，復大獲而旋。
units.en: Li Ju handed Zhi five hundred horses, split his force into three night columns, ran the enemy down, and came home laden with spoil.
units.literal: Li Ju thereupon gave Zhi five hundred horses, divided the army into three columns, pursued the bandits by night, and again took a great haul before returning.

units.zh: 先是，聰使其將趙固鎮洛陽，長史周振與固不協，密陳固罪。
units.en: Earlier Liu Cong had posted Zhao Gu at Luoyang; Zhou Zhen, Gu's chief of staff, hated him and denounced him in secret to the throne.
units.literal: Earlier, Liu Cong had sent his general Zhao Gu to garrison Luoyang; chief clerk Zhou Zhen was at odds with Gu and secretly reported Gu's crimes.

units.zh: 矩之破暢也，帳中得聰書，敕暢平矩訖，過洛陽，收固斬之，便以振代固。
units.en: In the rout of Liu Chang, Li Ju captured an order from Liu Cong telling Chang to finish off Li Ju, then swing through Luoyang, arrest Zhao Gu, put him to death, and install Zhou Zhen in his place.
units.literal: When Li Ju defeated Chang, in the tent he obtained a letter from Liu Cong instructing Chang, once Li Ju was pacified, to pass through Luoyang, seize Gu and execute him, and then replace Gu with Zhen.

units.zh: 矩送以示固，固即斬振父子，遂率騎一千來降，矩還令守洛。
units.en: Li Ju forwarded the letter to Zhao Gu, who at once beheaded Zhou Zhen and his sons, rode in with a thousand horse to defect, and was sent back to guard Luoyang.
units.literal: Li Ju sent it to show Gu; Gu immediately executed Zhen and his sons, then led a thousand horsemen to surrender; Li Ju ordered him back to hold Luoyang.

units.zh: 後數月，聰遣其太子粲率劉雅生等步騎十萬屯孟津北岸，分遣雅生攻趙固於洛。
units.en: Months later Liu Cong dispatched the crown prince Liu Can with Liu Yasheng and a host of one hundred thousand to the north shore at Mengjin, while Yasheng was sent to strike Zhao Gu in Luoyang.
units.literal: Several months later Liu Cong sent his heir Liu Can with Liu Yasheng and others, one hundred thousand foot and horse, to encamp on the north bank of the Meng ford, and separately sent Yasheng to attack Zhao Gu at Luoyang.

units.zh: 固奔陽城山，遣弟告急，矩遣郭誦屯洛口以救之。
units.en: Gu bolted to Yangcheng Mountain and begged for help; Li Ju stationed Guo Song at the Luo estuary to relieve him.
units.literal: Gu fled to Mount Yangcheng and sent his younger brother with an urgent plea; Li Ju sent Guo Song to hold the mouth of the Luo to relieve him.

units.zh: 誦使將張皮簡精卒千人夜渡河。
units.en: Guo Song told Zhang Pi to take a thousand elite men across the Yellow River under cover of dark.
units.literal: Song had his general Zhang Pi pick a thousand picked troops and cross the river by night.

units.zh: 粲候者告有兵至，粲恃其眾，不以為虞。
units.en: Liu Can's pickets reported an approaching force, but he trusted his mass of men and never tightened his guard.
units.literal: Can's scouts reported troops approaching; Can relied on his numbers and took no precautions.

units.zh: 既而誦等奄至，十道俱攻，粲眾驚擾，一時奔潰，殺傷太半，因據其營，獲其器械軍資不可勝數。
units.en: Then Guo Song struck from nowhere along ten fronts at once. Liu Can's army panicked and stampeded; over half were cut down. Song seized the camp and cartloads of arms and supplies beyond reckoning.
units.literal: Soon Song and the others arrived suddenly; they attacked on ten fronts at once; Can's host was thrown into panic and fled in rout at one stroke; more than half were killed or wounded; they therefore occupied his camp and captured weapons and military stores beyond counting.

units.zh: 及旦，粲見皮等人少，更與雅生悉餘眾攻之，苦戰二十餘日不能下。
units.en: At daybreak Liu Can saw how few Zhang Pi's men were and threw every survivor, with Yasheng, into a siege that ground on for twenty days without success.
units.literal: At dawn Can saw Pi and the others were few in number and again with Yasheng led all remaining troops against them; they fought bitterly more than twenty days but could not take them.

units.zh: 矩進救之，使壯士三千泛舟迎皮。
units.en: Li Ju marched to the rescue and floated three thousand picked men downriver to lift Zhang Pi out.
units.literal: Li Ju advanced to relieve them and sent three thousand stalwarts in boats to meet Pi.

units.zh: 賊臨河列陣，作長鉤以鉤船，連戰數日不得渡。
units.en: The enemy drew up along the bank and rigged long hooks to snare the boats; day after day of fighting still left Li Ju's men unable to cross.
units.literal: The bandits lined up along the river and fashioned long hooks to snag the boats; they fought several days and could not cross.

units.zh: 矩夜遣部將格增潛濟入皮壘，與皮選精騎千餘，而殺所獲牛馬，焚燒器械，夜穴圍而出，奔武牢。
units.en: Li Ju sent Ge Zeng by night to ford into Zhang Pi's ring; together they took a thousand crack horsemen, slaughtered the draft animals, torched their gear, burrowed through the lines after dark, and broke for Wulao.
units.literal: Li Ju by night sent subordinate general Ge Zeng to slip across and enter Pi's fort; with Pi he chose more than a thousand picked horsemen, then slaughtered the captured oxen and horses, burned the equipment, dug through the encirclement by night, broke out, and fled to Wulao.

units.zh: 聰追之，不及而退。
units.en: Liu Cong gave chase but could not catch them and turned back.
units.literal: Liu Cong pursued them, did not overtake them, and withdrew.

units.zh: 聰因憤恚，發病而死。
units.en: Liu Cong sickened with fury and died of it.
units.literal: Liu Cong thereupon, in rage and resentment, fell ill and died.

units.zh: 帝嘉其功，除矩都督河南三郡軍事、安西將軍、滎陽太守，封修武縣侯。
units.en: The court commended him, named him area commander for the three Henan commanderies with the titles General Who Pacifies the West and prefect of Xingyang, and created him marquis of Xiuwu.
units.literal: The emperor praised his merit, appointed Li Ju supervisor of military affairs for the three Henan commanderies, General Who Pacifies the West, and prefect of Xingyang, and enfeoffed him as marquis of Xiuwu county.

units.zh: 及劉粲嗣位，昏虐日甚，其將靳准乃起兵殺粲，並其宗族，發聰塚，斬其屍，遣使歸矩，稱「劉元海屠各小丑，因大晉事故之際，作亂幽并，矯稱天命，至令二帝幽沒虜庭。
units.en: Under Liu Can the throne turned ever more vicious and depraved until Jin Zhun mutinied, slaughtered Can and his kin, rifled Liu Cong's grave, mutilated the dead emperor's body, and wrote Li Ju that "Liu Yuan, that Tuge chieftain, used the Jin's collapse to riot through You and Bing while pretending to a mandate, leaving both our emperors rotting in alien hands,
units.literal: When Liu Can succeeded to the throne, his debauchery and cruelty grew daily; his general Jin Zhun thereupon raised troops, killed Can together with his whole clan, opened Liu Cong's tomb, hacked his corpse, and sent a messenger to Li Ju saying: "Liu Yuan of the Tuge was a petty bandit who, exploiting the Jin's misfortune, made trouble in You and Bing and falsely claimed Heaven's mandate, with the result that the two emperors languish captive in the barbarian court,

units.zh: 輒率眾扶侍梓宮，因請上聞」。
units.en: and I now march the army to escort the late emperors' catafalques and beg you to lay this before the Son of Heaven."
units.literal: I have led the host to escort the imperial coffins and therefore request that this be reported above."

units.zh: 矩馳表於帝，帝遣太常韓胤等奉迎梓宮，未至而准已為石勒、劉曜所沒。
units.en: Li Ju sent a flying memorial; the court dispatched Han Yin and others to meet the hearses, but before they arrived Jin Zhun had been crushed by Shi Le and Liu Yao.
units.literal: Li Ju galloped a memorial to the emperor; the emperor sent grand master of ceremonies Han Yin and others to welcome the coffins, but before they arrived Zhun had already been destroyed by Shi Le and Liu Yao.

units.zh: 矩以眾少不足立功，每慷慨憤歎。
units.en: His force was too slight to win lasting fame, and he often broke into bitter, helpless sighs.
units.literal: Li Ju, because his numbers were too few to accomplish merit, often sighed in generous indignation.

units.zh: 及帝踐阼，以為都督司州諸軍事、司州刺史，改封平陽縣侯，將軍如故。
units.en: At the new emperor's accession Li Ju became area commander for Si province and its inspector, traded his title for marquis of Pingyang county, and kept his old general's rank.
units.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, he appointed Li Ju supervisor of military affairs for Si province, inspector of Si province, changed his fief to county marquis of Pingyang, and his generalship remained as before.

units.zh: 時弘農太守尹安、振威將軍宋始等四軍並屯洛陽，各相疑阻，莫有固志。
units.en: Hongnong prefect Yin An, Song Shi the General Who Rouses Might, and two other columns all camped at Luoyang, eyeing one another with suspicion and no stomach for a stand.
units.literal: At that time prefect of Hongnong Yin An, General Who Rouses Might Song Shi, and four armies together were encamped at Luoyang; each suspected and blocked the others and none had a firm will to defend.

units.zh: 矩、默各遣千騎至洛以鎮之。
units.en: Li Ju and Guo Mo each detached a thousand riders to steady the garrison.
units.literal: Li Ju and Guo Mo each sent a thousand horsemen to Luoyang to stabilize them.

units.zh: 安等乃同謀告石勒，勒遣石生率騎五千至洛陽，矩、默軍皆退還。
units.en: Yin An and his fellows then jointly tipped off Shi Le, who sent Shi Sheng with five thousand horse; Li Ju and Guo Mo both pulled their men back.
units.literal: Yin An and the others then conspired together to inform Shi Le; Shi Le sent Shi Sheng with five thousand horsemen to Luoyang, and Li Ju's and Mo's armies both withdrew.

units.zh: 俄而四將復背勒，遣使乞迎，默又遣步卒五百人入洛。
units.en: Before long the four commanders turned on Shi Le again, begged for rescue, and Guo Mo pushed another five hundred foot into the city.
units.literal: Soon the four generals again betrayed Shi Le, sent envoys begging to be taken in, and Mo again sent five hundred foot soldiers into Luoyang.

units.zh: 石生以四將相謀，不能自安，乃虜宋始一軍，渡河而南。
units.en: Shi Sheng, unnerved by their collusion, seized Song Shi's whole command, forded south, and quit the city.
units.literal: Shi Sheng, because the four generals were plotting together, could not feel secure; he therefore captured Song Shi's entire army, crossed the river, and went south.

units.zh: 百姓相率歸矩，於是洛中遂空。
units.en: The townspeople streamed to Li Ju until Luoyang stood hollow.
units.literal: The common people in companies attached themselves to Li Ju, and thereby Luoyang became empty.

units.zh: 矩乃表郭誦為揚武將軍、陽翟令，阻水築壘，且耕且守，為滅賊之計。
units.en: He then recommended Guo Song for General Who Rouses Might and magistrate of Yangzhai; Guo Song relied on the water, built ramparts, and combined farming with defense as a plan to destroy the enemy.
units.literal: Li Ju thereupon memorialized recommending Guo Song as General Who Rouses Might and magistrate of Yangzhai; relying on the water, Guo Song built ramparts, simultaneously farming and defending, as a plan to destroy the bandits.

units.zh: 屬趙固死，石生遣騎襲誦，誦多計略，賊至，輒設伏破之，虜掠無所得。
units.en: When Zhao Gu died, Shi Sheng sent raiders against Guo Song, who was never short of tricks—each attack walked into an ambush and came away empty-handed.
units.literal: It happened that Zhao Gu died; Shi Sheng sent cavalry to raid Song; Song was full of stratagems—whenever the bandits came he laid ambushes and defeated them, and they obtained nothing from plundering.

units.zh: 生怒，又自率四千餘騎暴掠諸縣，因攻誦壘，接戰須臾，退軍堮阪。
units.en: Furious, Shi Sheng led over four thousand horse on a sweep of the countryside, then stormed Guo Song's walls; after a short clash he drew off to the Eban ridge.
units.literal: Sheng was angry and again personally led more than four thousand horsemen to ravage the counties, then attacked Song's fort; they joined battle briefly, then withdrew the army to the slope at Eban.

units.zh: 誦率勁勇五百追及生於磐脂故亭，又大破之。
units.en: Guo Song took five hundred of his best fighters, ran Shi Sheng down at the old Panzhi post station, and thrashed him again.
units.literal: Song led five hundred picked braves, overtook Sheng at the old pavilion of Panzhi, and again greatly defeated him.

units.zh: 矩以誦功多，表加赤幢曲蓋，封吉陽亭侯。
units.en: Li Ju cited Guo Song's heavy service and won him a crimson command canopy plus village marquis of Jiyang.
units.literal: Li Ju, because Song's merit was great, memorialized adding crimson canopy and curved cover and enfeoffing him as village marquis of Jiyang.

units.zh: 郭默欲侵祖約，矩禁之不可，遂為約所破。
units.en: Guo Mo meant to strike Zu Yue; Li Ju forbade it but could not hold him, and Mo was shattered.
units.literal: Guo Mo wished to invade Zu Yue; Li Ju forbade him but could not stop him, and he was therefore defeated by Yue.

units.zh: 石勒遣其養子匆襲默，默懼後患未已，將降于劉曜，遣參軍鄭雄詣矩謀之，矩距而不許。
units.en: Shi Le dispatched his foster son Shi Cong against him; dreading an endless vendetta, Guo Mo prepared to go over to Liu Yao and sent Zheng Xiong to sound Li Ju out, but Li Ju turned him down flat.
units.literal: Shi Le sent his adopted son Cong to raid Mo; Mo feared later troubles would not end and was about to surrender to Liu Yao; he sent adjutant Zheng Xiong to Li Ju to plan it, but Li Ju refused and would not permit it.

units.zh: 後勒遣其將石良率精兵五千襲矩，矩逆擊不利。
units.en: Later Shi Le sent Shi Liang with five thousand veterans against Li Ju, who met them head-on and lost.
units.literal: Later Shi Le sent his general Shi Liang with five thousand picked troops to raid Li Ju; Li Ju met them in a counterattack but fared badly.

units.zh: 郭誦弟元復為賊所執，賊遣元以書說矩曰：「去年東平曹嶷，西賓猗盧，矩如牛角，何不歸命？」
units.en: The enemy captured Guo Song's brother Yuan and sent him with a letter: "Eastward you feuded with Cao Yi of Dongping, westward you leaned on Yilu—you stand between them like a cow's horn—why not bend the knee?"
units.literal: Guo Song's younger brother Yuan was again taken by the bandits; the bandits sent Yuan with a letter to persuade Li Ju, saying: "Last year to the east you had Cao Yi of Dongping, to the west you guested Yilu—Li Ju, you are like a horn between them—why not submit to the command?"

units.zh: 矩以示誦，誦曰：「昔王陵母在賊，猶不改意，弟當何論！」
units.en: Li Ju showed Guo Song the letter. Song answered, "Wang Ling kept his loyalty even when his mother was hostage—why should a brother weigh more?"
units.literal: Li Ju showed it to Song; Song said: "In olden days Wang Ling's mother was in the enemy's hands and he still did not change his resolve—what is there to say of a younger brother!"

units.zh: 勒復遺誦麈尾馬鞭，以示殷勤，誦不答。
units.en: Shi Le followed with a flywhisk and whip as gifts of courtesy; Guo Song never answered.
units.literal: Shi Le again sent Song a horsetail flywhisk and riding crop to show earnest goodwill; Song did not reply.

units.zh: 勒將石生屯洛陽，大掠河南，矩、默大饑，默因復說矩降曜。
units.en: While Shi Sheng held Luoyang and stripped Henan bare, Li Ju and Guo Mo starved, and Mo again talked of defecting to Liu Yao.
units.literal: Shi Le's general Shi Sheng was encamped at Luoyang, greatly plundering Henan; Li Ju and Mo were in great famine, and Mo therefore again urged Li Ju to surrender to Yao.

units.zh: 矩既為石良所破,遂從默計，遣使於曜。
units.en: Broken by Shi Liang, Li Ju yielded to Guo Mo and sent feelers to Liu Yao.
units.literal: Li Ju, having already been defeated by Shi Liang, followed Mo's plan and sent envoys to Yao.

units.zh: 曜遣從弟岳軍于河陰，欲與矩謀攻石生。
units.en: Liu Yao posted his cousin Liu Yue on the north bank at Heyin to concert with Li Ju a strike on Shi Sheng.
units.literal: Yao sent his cousin Yue with an army at Heyin, wishing to join Li Ju in planning an attack on Shi Sheng.

units.zh: 勒遣將圍岳，嶽閉門不敢出。
units.en: Shi Le ringed Liu Yue with troops; Liu Yue shut his gates and refused to sortie.
units.literal: Shi Le sent generals to besiege Yue; Yue closed the gates and dared not come out.

units.zh: 默後為石匆所敗，自密南奔建康。
units.en: Guo Mo was later beaten by Shi Cong and ran south from Mi toward Jiankang.
units.literal: Mo was later defeated by Shi Cong and fled south from Mi to Jiankang.

units.zh: 矩聞之大怒，遣其將郭誦等齎書與默，又敕誦曰：「汝識脣亡之談不？
units.en: Li Ju, hearing of it, flew into a rage. He sent Guo Song with a letter for Guo Mo and warned him, "Have you forgotten how teeth and lips fall together?
units.literal: When Li Ju heard this he was greatly angry, sent his general Guo Song and others bearing a letter to Mo, and also instructed Song: "Do you understand the talk of lips and teeth perishing together?

units.zh: 迎接郭默，皆由於卿，臨難逃走，其必留之。」
units.en: You alone talked me into sheltering Guo Mo; now he has fled when danger came, and you must detain him."
units.literal: Our receiving Guo Mo was entirely because of you. Now that he has fled in the face of danger, you must detain him."

units.zh: 誦追及襄城，默自知負矩，棄妻子而遁。
units.en: Guo Song overtook him at Xiangcheng; knowing he had betrayed Li Ju, Guo Mo deserted his family and ran.
units.literal: Song overtook him at Xiangcheng; Mo, knowing he had wronged Li Ju, abandoned wife and children and fled.

units.zh: 誦擁其餘眾而歸，矩待其妻子如初。
units.en: Guo Song rounded up the stragglers and marched home; Li Ju sheltered Guo Mo's wife and children as before.
units.literal: Song gathered his remaining host and returned; Li Ju treated his wife and children as at first.

units.zh: 劉嶽以外援不至，降于石季龍。
units.en: With no relief column coming, Liu Yue yielded to Shi Hu.
units.literal: Liu Yue, because outer aid did not arrive, surrendered to Shi Jilong.

units.zh: 矩所統將士有陰欲歸勒者，矩知之而不能討，乃率眾南走，將歸朝廷，眾皆道亡，惟郭誦及參軍郭方，功曹張景，主簿苟遠，將軍騫韜、江霸、梁志、司馬尚、季弘、李瑰、段秀等百餘人棄家送矩。
units.en: Some of Li Ju's men were slipping away to Shi Le; he saw it but dared not purge them, so he struck south for the capital. The army melted away on the march until only Guo Song, Guo Fang, Zhang Jing, Gou Yuan, Qian Tao, Jiang Ba, Liang Zhi, Sima Shang, Ji Hong, Li Gui, Duan Xiu, and a hundred-odd loyalists forsook home to stay with him.
units.literal: Among the officers and soldiers Li Ju commanded, some secretly wished to join Shi Le; Li Ju knew it but could not punish them; he therefore led the host south, intending to return to the court; all along the road they deserted, and only Guo Song, adjutant Guo Fang, merit clerk Zhang Jing, secretary Gou Yuan, generals Qian Tao, Jiang Ba, Liang Zhi, Sima Shang, Ji Hong, Li Gui, Duan Xiu, and more than a hundred others abandoned their homes to escort Li Ju.

units.zh: 至於魯陽縣，矩墜馬卒，葬襄陽之峴山。
units.en: At Luyang he was thrown from his horse and died; they laid him on Xian Hill outside Xiangyang.
units.literal: When they reached Luyang county, Li Ju fell from a horse and died; he was buried on Xian Mountain at Xiangyang.

units.zh: 段匹磾
units.en: Duan Pidi
units.literal: Duan Pidi

units.zh: 段匹磾，東部鮮卑人也。
units.en: Duan Pidi belonged to the eastern branch of the Xianbei.
units.literal: Duan Pidi was a man of the eastern-branch Xianbei.

units.zh: 種類勁健，世為大人。
units.en: His people were fierce horsemen who for generations had ruled as chieftains.
units.literal: His kind was stalwart; for generations they had been great chiefs.

units.zh: 父務勿塵，遣軍助東海王越征討有功，王浚表為親晉王，封遼西公，嫁女與務勿塵，以結鄰援。
units.en: His father Wuwuchen had sent warriors to fight beside Prince Donghai Sima Yue; Wang Jun had him titled the Jin-allied king, created duke of Liaoxi, and married him a daughter to seal the frontier pact.
units.literal: His father Wuwuchen sent troops to aid Prince Donghai Sima Yue in campaigns and had merit; Wang Jun memorialized him as king friendly to the Jin, enfeoffed him duke of Liaoxi, married a daughter to Wuwuchen, and thereby cemented a neighboring alliance.

units.zh: 懷帝即位，以務勿塵為大單于，匹磾為左賢王，率眾助國征討，假撫軍大將軍。
units.en: Emperor Huai named Wuwuchen grand chanyu and Pidi left worthy king, brought their tribes in on imperial campaigns, and gave Pidi the acting title grand general who comforts the army.
units.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended the throne, he appointed Wuwuchen grand shanyu and Pidi left worthy king, led the host to aid the state in campaigns, and provisionally named him grand general who comforts the army.

units.zh: 務勿塵死，弟涉復辰以務勿塵子疾陸眷襲號。
units.en: When Wuwuchen died, his brother Shefuchen installed Wuwuchen's son Jilujuan as heir.
units.literal: When Wuwuchen died, his younger brother Shefuchen had Wuwuchen's son Jilujuan inherit the title.

units.zh: 劉曜逼洛陽，王浚遣督護王昌等率疾陸眷及弟文鴦、從弟末杯攻石勒于襄國。
units.en: As Liu Yao closed on Luoyang, Wang Jun dispatched Wang Chang to lead Jilujuan, Wenyang, and Mobo against Shi Le at Xiangguo.
units.literal: When Liu Yao pressed Luoyang, Wang Jun sent supervisor Wang Chang and others to lead Jilujuan and his younger brother Wenyang and cousin Mobo to attack Shi Le at Xiangguo.

units.zh: 勒敗還壘，末杯追入壘門，為勒所獲。
units.en: Shi Le fell back to his ramparts; Mobo chased through the gate and was taken alive.
units.literal: Le was defeated and returned to his fort; Mobo pursued into the fort gate and was captured by Le.

units.zh: 勒質末杯，遣使求和于疾陸眷，疾陸眷將許之，文鴦諫曰：「受命討勒，寧以末杯一人，故縱成擒之冠？
units.en: Shi Le held Mobo hostage and sued for peace; Jilujuan was ready to agree when Wenyang objected: "We were ordered to crush Shi Le—would you loose a cornered prey for one man?
units.literal: Le held Mobo hostage and sent an envoy to sue for peace with Jilujuan; Jilujuan was about to consent when Wenyang remonstrated: "We received orders to punish Shi Le—would you for Mobo alone release a foe already in the bag?

units.zh: 既失浚意，且有後憂，必不可許。」
units.en: You would forfeit Wang Jun's trust and court future peril—this must not be allowed."
units.literal: You will both lose Wang Jun's favor and afterward have later worries—it absolutely cannot be permitted."

units.zh: 疾陸眷不聽，以鎧馬二百五十匹、金銀各一簏贈末杯。
units.en: Jilujuan refused the counsel and sent two hundred fifty barded horses plus baskets of gold and silver to buy Mobo back.
units.literal: Jilujuan did not listen; he presented two hundred fifty armored horses and one basket each of gold and silver to ransom Mobo.

units.zh: 勒歸之，又厚以金寶采絹報疾陸眷。
units.en: Shi Le released him and heaped gold, gems, and brocades on Jilujuan in return.
units.literal: Le returned him and in turn richly repaid Jilujuan with gold, jewels, and colored silk.

units.zh: 疾陸眷令文鴦與石季龍同盟，約為兄弟，遂引騎還。
units.en: Jilujuan had Wenyang swear brotherhood with Shi Hu and then marched his cavalry home.
units.literal: Jilujuan ordered Wenyang to ally with Shi Jilong by oath as brothers, then led the horsemen back.

units.zh: 昌等不能獨守，亦還。
units.en: Wang Chang could not hold the field alone and withdrew as well.
units.literal: Chang and the others could not hold alone and likewise returned.

units.zh: 建武初，匹磾推劉琨為大都督，結盟討勒，並檄涉復辰、疾陸眷、末杯等三面俱集襄國，琨、匹磾進屯固安，以候眾軍。
units.en: Early in the Jianwu era Pidi raised Liu Kun to supreme commander, forged a league against Shi Le, and called Shefuchen, Jilujuan, and Mobo to converge on Xiangguo from three directions while he and Liu Kun camped at Gu'an to wait for them.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, Pidi promoted Liu Kun as grand commander-in-chief, formed an alliance to punish Shi Le, and jointly summoned Shefuchen, Jilujuan, Mobo, and others so that three sides would all gather at Xiangguo; Kun and Pidi advanced and encamped at Gu'an to await the assembled armies.

units.zh: 勒懼，遣間使厚賂末杯。
units.en: Shi Le, alarmed, slipped Mobo a heavy bribe through a covert messenger.
units.literal: Le feared and sent a secret envoy with rich bribes to Mobo.

units.zh: 然末杯既思報其舊恩，且因匹磾在外，欲襲奪其國，乃間匹磾於涉復辰、疾陸眷曰：「以父兄而從子弟邪？
units.en: Mobo meant both to repay an old debt and, with Pidi away, to seize his domain; he whispered to Shefuchen and Jilujuan, "Why should fathers and elder brothers take orders from sons and younger brothers?
units.literal: Yet Mobo both wished to repay an old kindness and, moreover, because Pidi was abroad, wished to seize his state by surprise; he therefore slandered Pidi to Shefuchen and Jilujuan, saying: "Should fathers and elder brothers follow sons and younger brothers?

units.zh: 雖一旦有功，匹磾獨收之矣。」
units.en: Even if the day brings victory, Pidi alone will pocket the glory."
units.literal: Even if in one morning there is merit, Pidi alone will harvest it."

units.zh: 涉復辰等以為然，引軍而還。
units.en: Shefuchen and his kin thought him right and marched home.
units.literal: Shefuchen and the others held it right and led the army back.

units.zh: 匹磾亦止。
units.en: Pidi too stopped in his tracks.
units.literal: Pidi likewise halted.

units.zh: 會疾陸眷病死，匹磾自薊奔喪，至於右北平。
units.en: When Jilujuan died, Pidi raced from Ji to the funeral and reached Youbeiping.
units.literal: It happened that Jilujuan died of illness; Pidi from Ji hurried to the mourning and reached Youbeiping.

units.zh: 末杯宣言匹磾將篡，出軍擊敗之。
units.en: Mobo accused Pidi of plotting usurpation, took the field, and broke his force.
units.literal: Mobo publicly declared Pidi was about to usurp, marched out, and defeated him.

units.zh: 末杯遂害涉復辰及其子弟黨與二百餘人，自立為單于。
units.en: He then slaughtered Shefuchen, over two hundred sons and followers, and declared himself chanyu.
units.literal: Mobo thereupon killed Shefuchen and more than two hundred of his sons, younger kin, and faction, and established himself as shanyu.

units.zh: 及王浚敗，匹磾領幽州刺史，劉琨自并州依之，復與匹磾結盟，俱討石勒。
units.en: After Wang Jun's fall Pidi became inspector of You; Liu Kun came down from Bing to lean on him, and the two renewed their pact against Shi Le.
units.literal: When Wang Jun was defeated, Pidi took the office of inspector of You province; Liu Kun from Bing province relied on him and again allied with Pidi, both together campaigning against Shi Le.

units.zh: 匹磾復為末杯所敗，士眾離散，懼琨圖己，遂害之，於是晉人離散矣。
units.en: Pidi lost again to Mobo and his army melted away; dreading Liu Kun's designs, he murdered him, and the Chinese followers drifted away.
units.literal: Pidi was again defeated by Mobo; his soldiers and host scattered; fearing Kun would plot against him, he thereupon killed him, and thereby Jin people scattered apart.

units.zh: 匹磾不能自固，北依邵續，末杯又攻敗之。
units.en: Unable to stand alone, Pidi fled north to Shao Xu; Mobo struck him once more and broke him.
units.literal: Pidi could not secure himself and fled north to rely on Shao Xu; Mobo again attacked and defeated him.

units.zh: 匹磾被瘡，謂續曰：「吾夷狄慕義，以至破家，君若不忘舊要，與吾進討，君之惠也。」
units.en: Wounded, Pidi told Shao Xu, "We steppe folk clung to honor until our houses were ruined; if you still honor our old pledge and march with me against the foe, you will do me the greatest kindness."
units.literal: Pidi, wounded, said to Xu: "We barbarians admired righteousness until our families were broken; if you do not forget the old compact and join me in advancing the punishment, it will be your grace."

units.zh: 續曰：「賴公威德，續得效節。
units.en: Shao Xu replied, "It was your prestige that let me serve the throne at all.
units.literal: Xu said: "Relying on your awesome virtue, Xu was able to devote his utmost loyalty.

units.zh: 今公有難，豈敢不俱！」
units.en: Now you are in peril—how could I hang back?"
units.literal: Now the lord is in difficulty—how could I dare not go together!"

units.zh: 遂並力追末杯，斬獲略盡。
units.en: They joined forces, ran Mobo down, and killed or captured almost every man.
units.literal: Thereupon they joined strength pursuing Mobo, killing and capturing nearly all.

units.zh: 又令文鴦北討末杯弟于薊城，及還，去城八十里，聞續已沒，眾懼而散，復為石季龍所遮，文鴦以其親兵數百人力戰破之，始得入城。
units.en: He sent Wenyang north against Mobo's brother at Ji; on the way back, eighty li from the walls, word came that Shao Xu had fallen—the army panicked and broke. Shi Hu barred the road, but Wenyang cut through with a few hundred household guards and fought his way inside.
units.literal: He also ordered Wenyang north to punish Mobo's younger brother at Ji city; when returning, eighty li from the city, hearing Xu had already been lost, the host feared and scattered, and again was intercepted by Shi Jilong; Wenyang with several hundred of his personal guard fought bitterly, broke them, and only then was able to enter the city.

units.zh: 季龍復抄城下，文鴦登城臨見，欲出擊之，匹磾不許。
units.en: Shi Hu raided the suburbs again; Wenyang mounted the wall, itching to sortie, but Pidi forbade it.
units.literal: Shi Jilong again raided beneath the walls; Wenyang ascended the walls and looked down, wishing to go out and strike them, but Pidi did not permit it.

units.zh: 文鴦曰：「我以勇聞，故百姓杖我。
units.en: Wenyang said, "My name is courage—the people lean on me for that.
units.literal: Wenyang said: "I am famed for courage; therefore the common people lean on me.

units.zh: 見人被略而不救，非丈夫也。
units.en: To watch folk dragged away and do nothing is unworthy of a man.
units.literal: To see people carried off and not rescue them is not the conduct of a man.

units.zh: 令眾失望，誰復為我致死乎！」
units.en: If the army loses heart, who will die for me again?"
units.literal: If the host loses hope, who again will die for me!"

units.zh: 遂將壯士數十騎出戰，殺胡甚多。
units.en: He led several dozen picked horsemen out and piled Hu corpses high.
units.literal: Thereupon he led several tens of stalwart horsemen out to battle and killed very many Hu.

units.zh: 遇馬乏，伏不能起。
units.en: His mount gave out, collapsed, and could not rise.
units.literal: His horse grew exhausted, collapsed, and could not rise.

units.zh: 季龍呼曰：「大兄與我俱是戎狄，久望共同。
units.en: Shi Hu shouted, "We are both steppe men; I have long wanted us on the same side.
units.literal: Shi Jilong called out: "Elder brother and I are both Rong and Di; for long I have hoped we might share the same path.

units.zh: 天不違願，今日相見，何故復戰？
units.en: Heaven grants the meeting—why trade blows now?
units.literal: Heaven has not opposed the wish—today we meet face to face; for what reason do we fight again?

units.zh: 請釋杖。」
units.en: Drop your lance."
units.literal: Please lay down the staff."

units.zh: 文鴦罵曰：「汝為寇虐，久應合死，吾兄不用吾計，故令汝得至此，吾寧死，不為汝擒。」
units.en: Wenyang snarled back, "You have ravaged like a wolf and earned death a hundred times; my brother spurned my counsel and let you come this far—I will die before I let you take me."
units.literal: Wenyang cursed him: "You have acted the bandit tyrant and long ago deserved death; my elder brother did not use my plan, therefore he let you reach this point; I would rather die than be captured by you."

units.zh: 遂下馬苦戰，槊折，執刀力戰不已。
units.en: He leapt down to fight on foot; his spear snapped, so he seized a knife and kept slashing.
units.literal: Thereupon he dismounted and fought bitterly on foot; his lance broke; grasping a knife he fought on without stopping.

units.zh: 季龍軍四面解馬羅披自鄣，前捉文鴦。
units.en: Shi Hu's men ringed him with horse ropes and leather screens, then closed to seize him.
units.literal: Shi Jilong's army on four sides loosened horse nets and leather screens to shield themselves and advanced to seize Wenyang.

units.zh: 文鴦戰自辰至申，力極而後被執。
units.en: He fought from dawn past noon until strength failed and they took him.
units.literal: Wenyang fought from the chen hour to the shen hour; only when his strength was exhausted was he at last captured.

units.zh: 城內大懼。
units.en: Panic swept the walls.
units.literal: Inside the city there was great fear.

units.zh: 匹磾欲單騎歸朝，續弟樂安內史洎協兵，不許，洎復欲執臺使王英送于季龍，匹磾正色責之曰：「卿不能遵兄之志，逼吾不得歸朝，亦以甚矣，復欲執天子使者，我雖胡素，所未聞也。」
units.en: Duan Pidi meant to ride alone to the Jin court, but Shao Xu's brother Ji, interior governor of Le'an, mobilized troops and barred the way; Ji even meant to seize imperial envoy Wang Ying and hand him to Shi Hu. Pidi rebuked him coldly: "You refuse your brother's purpose and block me from the capital—that is bad enough; now you would lay hands on the emperor's messenger. I am a barbarian by blood, yet even I have never heard the like."
units.literal: Pidi wished to ride alone to the court; Shao Xu's younger brother, interior governor of Le'an, Ji, coordinated troops and would not permit it; Ji again wished to seize court envoy Wang Ying and deliver him to Shi Jilong; Pidi with stern countenance rebuked him, saying: "You cannot follow your elder brother's will, forcing me so I cannot return to the court—that is already extreme; again you wish to seize the Son of Heaven's envoy—although I am a Hu by birth, I have never heard of such a thing."

units.zh: 因謂英曰：「匹磾世受重恩，不忘忠孝。
units.en: Turning to Wang Ying he said, "My house has eaten the Jin's bounty for generations; we have not forgotten loyalty or duty.
units.literal: Thereupon he said to Ying: "Pidi's family for generations has received heavy favor and does not forget loyalty and filial piety.

units.zh: 今日事逼，欲歸罪朝廷，而見逼迫，忠款不遂。
units.en: Circumstances drive me now—I would lay my guilt before the throne, yet I am hemmed in until my good faith cannot reach it.
units.literal: Today affairs press me; I wished to return to the court to answer for my guilt, yet I am pressed and blocked; my loyal sincerity cannot be fulfilled.

units.zh: 若得假息，未死之日，心不忘本。」
units.en: If I gain a little breathing space, I shall not forget where I came from while I still draw breath."
units.literal: If I can obtain borrowed rest, on days before death my heart will not forget its root."

units.zh: 遂渡黃河南。
units.en: He then forded the Yellow River to the south.
units.literal: Thereupon he crossed the Yellow River southward.

units.zh: 匹磾著朝服，持節，賓從出見季龍曰：「我受國恩，志在滅汝。
units.en: In full court dress, baton in hand, he stepped out with his train to face Shi Hu and said, "The dynasty favored me; I meant to destroy you.
units.literal: Pidi put on court robes, grasped the credential, and with guests and followers went out to see Shi Jilong, saying: "I received the state's grace; my will was to destroy you.

units.zh: 不幸吾國自亂，以至於此。
units.en: My own people tore themselves apart until we came to this pass.
units.literal: Unluckily my state fell into internal disorder, so that it reached this point.

units.zh: 既不能死，又不能為汝敬也。」
units.en: I can neither die a clean death nor bow to you."
units.literal: I can neither die nor bow in respect to you."

units.zh: 勒及季龍素與匹磾結為兄弟，季龍起而拜之。
units.en: Shi Le and Shi Hu had once sworn brotherhood with him; Shi Hu rose and bowed.
units.literal: Shi Le and Shi Jilong had of old sworn brotherhood with Pidi; Shi Jilong rose and bowed to him.

units.zh: 匹磾到襄國，又不為勒禮，常著朝服，持晉節。
units.en: At Xiangguo he still refused to humble himself before Shi Le, going about in Jin court dress with the Jin baton in hand.
units.literal: When Pidi arrived at Xiangguo, again he did not perform courtesy to Shi Le; he constantly wore court robes and held the Jin credential.

units.zh: 經年，國中謀推匹磾為主，事露，被害。
units.en: A year later a plot to make him ruler came to light and he was executed.
units.literal: After a full year, in the state a plot to promote Pidi as lord leaked out, and he was killed.

units.zh: 文鴦亦遇鴆而死，惟末波存焉。
units.en: Wenyang too was poisoned; only Mobo was left alive.
units.literal: Wenyang likewise met death by poisoned wine; only Mobo survived.

units.zh: 及死，弟牙立。
units.en: When Mobo died, his brother Ya inherited.
units.literal: When he died, his younger brother Ya succeeded.

units.zh: 牙死，其後從祖就陸眷之孫遼立。
units.en: Ya's death left the chieftaincy to Liao, a grandson of the Jiulujuan branch.
units.literal: When Ya died, afterward Liao, grandson of Jiulujuan on the collateral line, succeeded.

units.zh: 自務勿塵已後，值晉喪亂，自稱位號，據有遼西之地，而臣禦晉人。
units.en: From Wuwuchen's day through the Jin collapse they styled themselves kings, held western Liaoxi, and governed their Chinese subjects in feudal order.
units.literal: From Wuwuchen onward, encountering the Jin's ruin and chaos, they styled themselves with titles and ranks, occupied the land west of Liaoxi, and ruled over Jin people as subjects.

units.zh: 其地西盡幽州，東界遼水。
units.en: Their realm ran west to the edge of You and east to the Liao River.
units.literal: Their territory reached west to the limit of You province and east bordered the Liao River.

units.zh: 然所統胡晉可三萬餘家，控弦可四五萬騎，而與石季龍遞相侵掠，連兵不息，竟為季龍所破，徙其遺黎數萬家于司雍之地。
units.en: They counted some thirty thousand Hu and Chinese households and forty or fifty thousand archers on horseback, yet they skirmished endlessly with Shi Hu until he broke them and deported tens of thousands of survivors into Si and Yong.
units.literal: Yet those they ruled, Hu and Jin together, were more than thirty thousand households; bowstrings drawn could be forty or fifty thousand horsemen; yet with Shi Jilong they repeatedly raided each other in turn; arms did not cease; in the end they were broken by Shi Jilong, who moved their surviving common people, several tens of thousands of households, to the lands of Si and Yong.

units.zh: 其子蘭復聚兵，與季龍為患久之。
units.en: His son Lan rallied another army and plagued Shi Hu for years.
units.literal: His son Lan again gathered troops and for a long time was a trouble to Shi Jilong.

units.zh: 及石氏之亡，末波之子勤鳩集胡羯得萬餘人，保枉人山，自稱趙王，附于慕容俊。
units.en: After the Shi fell, Mobo's son Qin mustered over ten thousand Hu and Jie on Mount Wangren, declared himself king of Zhao, and submitted to Murong Jun.
units.literal: When the Shi clan perished, Mobo's son Qin gathered Hu and Jie to more than ten thousand men, held Mount Wangren, styled himself king of Zhao, and attached himself to Murong Jun.

units.zh: 俄為冉閔所敗，徙於繹幕，僭即尊號。
units.en: Ran Min soon broke him and drove him to Yimu, where he claimed the imperial style.
units.literal: Soon he was defeated by Ran Min and moved to Yimu, usurping the supreme title.

units.zh: 俊遣慕容恪擊之，勤懼而降。
units.en: Murong Jun sent Murong Ke against him; Qin yielded in terror.
units.literal: Jun sent Murong Ke to strike him; Qin feared and surrendered.

units.zh: 魏浚
units.en: Wei Jun
units.literal: Wei Jun

units.zh: 魏浚，東郡東阿人也，寓居關中。
units.en: Wei Jun came from Dong'e in Dong Commandery but had settled in Guanzhong.
units.literal: Wei Jun was a man of Dong'e in Dong commandery and sojourned in Guanzhong.

units.zh: 初為雍州小吏，河間王顒敗亂之際，以為武威將軍。
units.en: He began as a minor clerk in Yong; amid Prince Hejian Sima Yong's defeat he was named General Who Displays Might.
units.literal: At first he was a petty clerk in Yong province; during the defeat and turmoil of Prince Hejian Sima Yong, he was appointed General Who Displays Might.

units.zh: 後為度支校尉，有幹用。
units.en: He rose to commissary colonel and proved capable in office.
units.literal: Later he became commissary colonel and had administrative ability.

units.zh: 永嘉末，與流人數百家東保河陰之硤石。
units.en: Late in the Yongjia era he led several hundred refugee families east to hold the Xiashi defile north of the river.
units.literal: At the end of Yongjia, with several hundred households of displaced persons he went east to protect Xiashi on the Yin of the Yellow River's north bank.

units.zh: 時京邑荒儉，浚劫掠得穀麥，獻之懷帝，帝以為揚威將軍、平陽太守，度支如故。
units.en: The capital was starving; Wei Jun seized grain and sent it to Emperor Huai, who named him General Who Displays Might and prefect of Pingyang while keeping him on supply duty.
units.literal: At that time the capital district was desolate and straitened; Jun by plunder obtained grain and wheat, presented them to Emperor Huai, and the emperor appointed him General Who Displays Might and prefect of Pingyang, his commissary post remaining as before.

units.zh: 以亂不之官。
units.en: The chaos kept him from taking his post.
units.literal: Because of the turmoil he did not take up the office.

units.zh: 及洛陽陷，屯於洛北石梁塢，撫養遺眾，漸修軍器。
units.en: After Luoyang fell he garrisoned Shiliang Fort north of the Luo, supported the survivors, and gradually repaired military equipment.
units.literal: When Luoyang fell, he encamped north of the Luo at the Stone Beam fort, comforted the surviving host, and gradually repaired military equipment.

units.zh: 其附賊者，皆先解喻，說大晉運數靈長，行已建立，歸之者甚眾。
units.en: To those who had served the rebels he preached that the great Jin still enjoyed Heaven's favor and a new emperor already sat on the throne; multitudes came back.
units.literal: Those who had attached to the bandits he first explained and persuaded, declaring the great Jin's fortune long and numinous and that the ruler had already been established; those who returned were very many.

units.zh: 其有恃遠不從命者，遣將討之，服從而已，不加侵暴。
units.en: Defiant holdouts he chastised by arms, then stopped the moment they yielded, without needless cruelty.
units.literal: Those who relied on distance and did not obey orders he sent generals to punish; once they submitted he stopped and did not add invasion or violence.

units.zh: 於是遠近感悅，繈負至者漸眾。
units.en: Word spread, and refugees with children on their backs streamed to him.
units.literal: Thereby near and far were moved and pleased, and those who arrived carrying infants on their backs gradually grew numerous.

units.zh: 劉琨承制，假浚河南尹。
units.en: Liu Kun in plenipotentiary orders made him acting metropolitan governor of Henan.
units.literal: Liu Kun, exercising plenipotentiary command, provisionally appointed Jun metropolitan governor of Henan.

units.zh: 時太尉荀籓建行臺在密縣，浚詣籓諮謀軍事，籓甚悅，要李矩同會。
units.en: Grand commandant Xun Fan had a field headquarters at Mi; Wei Jun rode there to plan strategy. Fan was delighted and asked Li Ju to join the council.
units.literal: At that time grand commandant Xun Fan had set up a mobile headquarters at Mi county; Jun went to Fan to consult on military affairs; Fan was greatly pleased and invited Li Ju to meet together.

units.zh: 矩將夜赴之，矩官屬以浚不可信，不宜夜往。
units.en: Li Ju meant to travel by night, but his staff said Wei Jun was untrustworthy and a night ride unwise.
units.literal: Ju was about to go by night; Ju's subordinates held that Jun could not be trusted and it was not fitting to go by night.

units.zh: 矩曰：「忠臣同心，將何疑乎！」
units.en: Li Ju answered, "Loyal men share one mind—what is there to fear!"
units.literal: Ju said: "Loyal ministers share one heart—what is there to doubt!

units.zh: 及會，客主盡歎，浚因與矩相結而去。
units.en: At the meeting host and guests were moved alike; Wei Jun and Li Ju swore friendship and parted.
units.literal: When they met, guest and host all sighed in admiration; Jun therefore formed ties with Ju and departed.

units.zh: 劉曜忌浚得眾，率眾軍圍之。
units.en: Liu Yao, jealous of his following, brought an army to besiege him.
units.literal: Liu Yao resented Jun's winning the host and led an army to besiege him.

units.zh: 劉演、郭默遣軍來救，曜分兵逆于河北，乃伏兵深隱處，以邀演、默軍，大破之，盡虜演等騎。
units.en: Liu Yan and Guo Mo sent relief, but Liu Yao split a force to block the north bank, laid an ambush in rough country, shattered the column, and took every horseman of Yan's command.
units.literal: Liu Yan and Guo Mo sent troops to relieve him; Yao divided troops to intercept north of the River, then ambushed in a deeply hidden place to intercept Yan's and Mo's army, greatly defeated them, and fully captured Yan and the others' cavalry.

units.zh: 浚夜遁走，為曜所得，遂死之。
units.en: Wei Jun slipped away at night, fell into Liu Yao's hands, and died there.
units.literal: Jun fled by night, was taken by Yao, and thereupon died at his hands.

units.zh: 追贈平西將軍。
units.en: The court posthumously named him General Who Pacifies the West.
units.literal: He was posthumously awarded General Who Pacifies the West.

units.zh: 族子該領其眾。
units.en: His kinsman Wei Gai took command of the remnant.
units.literal: His agnate nephew Gai led his host.

units.zh: 族子該
units.en: Kinsman Wei Gai
units.literal: Agnate nephew Gai

units.zh: =該一名亥，本僑居京兆陰磐。
units.en: Wei Gai was also called Hai and had lived as a sojourner at Yinpan in Jingzhao.
units.literal: = Gai's other name was Hai; originally he sojourned at Yinpan in Jingzhao.

units.zh: 河間王顒之伐趙王倫，以該為將兵都尉。
units.en: When Prince Hejian marched against Prince Zhao, Sima Lun, he named Wei Gai colonel of troops.
units.literal: When Prince Hejian Sima Yong campaigned against Prince Zhao Sima Lun, he appointed Gai colonel commanding troops.

units.zh: 及劉曜攻洛陽，隨浚赴難，先領兵守金墉城，故得無他。
units.en: During Liu Yao's siege of Luoyang he rode with Wei Jun to the rescue and held the Metal Moat first, thereby escaping harm.
units.literal: When Liu Yao attacked Luoyang, he followed Jun to answer the crisis, first leading troops to defend the Metal Moat fort, and therefore escaped harm.

units.zh: 曜引去，餘眾依之。
units.en: When Liu Yao drew off, the survivors rallied to him.
units.literal: Yao led his forces away; the remaining host relied on him.

units.zh: 時杜預子尹為弘農太守，屯宜陽界一泉塢，數為諸賊所抄掠。
units.en: Du Yu's son Yin held Hongnong from the Yiquan fort on the Yiyang border and suffered repeated bandit raids.
units.literal: At that time Du Yin, son of Du Yu, was prefect of Hongnong, encamped at the Yiquan fort on the Yiyang border, and several times was raided by various bandits.

units.zh: 尹要該共距之，該遣其將馬瞻將三百人赴尹。
units.en: Du Yin called on Wei Gai for help; Gai sent Ma Zhan with three hundred men.
units.literal: Yin invited Gai jointly to resist them; Gai sent his general Ma Zhan with three hundred men to go to Yin.

units.zh: 瞻知其無備，夜襲尹殺之，迎該據塢。
units.en: Ma Zhan saw the garrison was slack, stormed it by night, murdered Du Yin, and installed Wei Gai in the fort.
units.literal: Zhan knew he was unprepared, raided Yin by night, killed him, and welcomed Gai to occupy the fort.

units.zh: 塢人震懼，並服從之。
units.en: The defenders were terrified into submission.
units.literal: The people of the fort were shaken with fear and all submitted to him.

units.zh: 乃與李炬、郭默相結以距賊。
units.en: He then allied with Li Ju and Guo Mo against the rebels.
units.literal: Thereupon he formed ties with Li Ju and Guo Mo jointly to resist the bandits.

units.zh: 荀籓即以該為武威將軍，統城西雍涼人，使討劉曜。
units.en: Xun Fan at once named him General Who Displays Might over the western Yong and Liang communities and sent him against Liu Yao.
units.literal: Xun Fan immediately appointed Gai General Who Displays Might, commanding the Yong and Liang people west of the city, and had him campaign against Liu Yao.

units.zh: 元帝承制，加冠軍將軍、河東太守。
units.en: Emperor Yuan in acting authority added General Who Crowns the Army and prefect of Hedong.
units.literal: Emperor Yuan, exercising plenipotentiary command, added General Who Crowns the Army and prefect of Hedong.

units.zh: 督護河東、河南、平陽三郡。
units.en: He was given staff authority over Hedong, Henan, and Pingyang.
units.literal: Chief of staff for Hedong, Henan, and Pingyang three commanderies.

units.zh: 曜嘗攻李矩，該破之。
units.en: When Liu Yao struck Li Ju, Wei Gai broke his attack.
units.literal: Yao once attacked Li Ju; Gai defeated him.

units.zh: 及矩將迎郭默，該遣軍助之，又與河南尹任愔相連結。
units.en: He sent troops to help Li Ju escort Guo Mo and joined Henan governor Ren Yin.
units.literal: When Ju was about to welcome Guo Mo, Gai sent troops to aid him, and again he linked with metropolitan governor of Henan Ren Yin.

units.zh: 後漸饑弊，曜寇日至，欲率眾南徙，眾不從，該遂單騎走至南陽。
units.en: Starvation and Liu Yao's daily raids wore them down; when Wei Gai tried to move the army south, the men refused, and he fled alone to Nanyang.
units.literal: Later they gradually grew hungry and exhausted; Yao's raids came daily; he wished to lead the host south to migrate; the host would not follow; Gai thereupon alone on horseback fled to Nanyang.

units.zh: 帝又以為前鋒都督、平北將軍、雍州刺史。
units.en: The court named him vanguard commander, General Who Pacifies the North, and inspector of Yong.
units.literal: The emperor again appointed him vanguard area commander, General Who Pacifies the North, and inspector of Yong province.

units.zh: 馬瞻率該餘眾降曜。
units.en: Ma Zhan led what was left of his force to Liu Yao.
units.literal: Ma Zhan led Gai's remaining host and surrendered to Yao.

units.zh: 曜徵發既苦，瞻又驕虐，部曲遣使呼該，該密往赴之，其眾殺瞻而納該。
units.en: Liu Yao's conscriptions had crushed the men, and Ma Zhan ruled them with cruelty until his officers secretly called Wei Gai back; they killed Ma Zhan and restored Gai.
units.literal: Yao's levies were already bitter; Zhan again was arrogant and cruel; retainers sent envoys to summon Gai; Gai secretly went to join them; his host killed Zhan and welcomed Gai.

units.zh: 該遷於新野，率眾助周訪討平杜曾，詔以該為順陽太守。
units.en: He withdrew to Xinye, marched with Zhou Fang to crush Du Zeng, and was appointed prefect of Shunyang.
units.literal: Gai moved to Xinye, led the host to aid Zhou Fang in punishing and pacifying Du Zeng, and an edict appointed Gai prefect of Shunyang.

units.zh: 王敦之反也，梁州刺史甘卓不從，欲觀該去就，試以敦旨動之。
units.en: When Wang Dun rose, Gan Zhuo of Liang province did not join him and, wishing to test Wei Gai's allegiance, sounded him with an order from Dun.
