units.literal: When Wang Dun rebelled, inspector of Liang province Gan Zhuo did not follow; wishing to observe Gai's course, he tested him by moving him with Dun's order.

units.zh: 該曰：「我本去賊，惟忠於國。
units.en: Wei Gai replied, "I left the rebels to serve the throne alone.
units.literal: Gai said: "I originally left the bandits—only loyalty to the state.

units.zh: 今王公舉兵向天子，非吾所宜與也。」
units.en: Now a prince marches on the emperor—nothing could make me take his part."
units.literal: Now the prince duke raises troops against the Son of Heaven—it is not what I ought to join."

units.zh: 遂距而不應。
units.en: He refused outright.
units.literal: Thereupon he refused and did not respond.

units.zh: 及蘇峻反，率眾救臺，軍次石頭，受陶侃節度。
units.en: When Su Jun mutinied he brought his men to relieve the palace, halted at Stone City, and served under Tao Kan.
units.literal: When Su Jun rebelled, he led the host to rescue the terrace palaces; the army halted at Stone Fort and received Tao Kan's command.

units.zh: 峻未平，該病篤還屯，卒於道，葬于武陵。
units.en: Su Jun was still in the field when Wei Gai, mortally ill, turned for his camp, died on the march, and was buried at Wuling.
units.literal: Before Jun was pacified, Gai, gravely ill, returned to encampment, died on the road, and was buried at Wuling.

units.zh: 從子雄統其眾。
units.en: His nephew Wei Xiong inherited the command.
units.literal: His agnate nephew Xiong commanded his host.

units.zh: 郭默
units.en: Guo Mo
units.literal: Guo Mo

units.zh: 郭默，河內懷人。
units.en: Guo Mo came from Huai in Henei.
units.literal: Guo Mo was a man of Huai in Henei.

units.zh: 少微賤，以壯勇事太守裴整，為督將。
units.en: Born poor, he won a place through sheer nerve as a staff commander under Prefect Pei Zheng.
units.literal: In youth he was lowly and mean; with stalwart courage he served prefect Pei Zheng as chief of staff.

units.zh: 永嘉之亂，默率遺眾自為塢主，以漁舟抄東歸行旅，積年遂致巨富，流人依附者漸眾。
units.en: When Yongjia tore the realm apart he made himself lord of a river fort, robbed eastbound travelers from boats, grew rich over the years, and drew a swelling crowd of refugees.
units.literal: In the Yongjia turmoil, Mo led the surviving host and made himself fort chief; using fishing boats he plundered eastbound travelers on the river; over years he thereby became enormously wealthy, and displaced persons who attached themselves gradually grew numerous.

units.zh: 撫循將士，甚得其歡心。
units.en: He knew how to handle his soldiers and kept their loyalty.
units.literal: He comforted and guided officers and men and very much won their hearts.

units.zh: 默婦兄同郡陸嘉取官米數石餉妹，默以為違制，將殺嘉，嘉懼，奔石勒。
units.en: His brother-in-law Lu Jia stole a few sacks of government grain for Mo's wife; Mo called it a capital offense. Lu Jia ran to Shi Le for his life.
units.literal: Mo's wife's elder brother from the same commandery, Lu Jia, took several shi of official rice to feed his younger sister; Mo held it violated regulations and was about to kill Jia; Jia feared and fled to Shi Le.

units.zh: 默乃自射殺婦，以明無私。
units.en: To prove his impartiality he shot his own wife dead.
units.literal: Mo thereupon personally shot and killed his wife to show he had no private partiality.

units.zh: 遣使謁劉琨，琨加默河內太守。
units.en: He sent envoys to Liu Kun, who named him prefect of Henei.
units.literal: He sent an envoy to visit Liu Kun; Kun appointed Mo prefect of Henei.

units.zh: 劉元海遣從子曜討默，曜列三屯圍之，欲使餓死。
units.en: Liu Yuan sent Liu Yao against him; Yao ringed him with three camps and tried to starve him out.
units.literal: Liu Yuanhai sent his nephew Yao to punish Mo; Yao set three camps to besiege him, wishing to starve him to death.

units.zh: 默送妻子為質，並請糴焉，糴畢，設守。
units.en: He handed over his family as hostages, bought grain, then threw up defenses the moment the grain was in.
units.literal: Mo sent wife and children as hostages and also requested to buy grain; when the purchase was finished, he set defenses.

units.zh: 曜怒，沈默妻子于河而攻之。
units.en: Liu Yao, furious, drowned his hostages and stormed the fort.
units.literal: Yao was angry, drowned Mo's wife and children in the river, and attacked him.

units.zh: 默遣弟芝求救于劉琨，琨知默狡猾，留之而緩其救。
units.en: Guo Mo sent his brother Zhi to Liu Kun for help; Kun, knowing Mo's cunning, held Zhi back and slow-walked the relief.
units.literal: Mo sent his younger brother Zhi to beg rescue from Liu Kun; Kun, knowing Mo was treacherous, detained him and delayed the rescue.

units.zh: 默更遣人告急。
units.en: Mo sent fresh pleas for aid.
units.literal: Mo again sent men with urgent plea.

units.zh: 會芝出城浴馬，使強與俱歸。
units.en: When Zhi rode outside to water the horses, Mo had him seized and dragged back in.
units.literal: It happened that Zhi left the city to bathe horses; Mo had someone force him to return together.

units.zh: 默乃遣芝質于石勒，勒以默多詐，封默書與劉曜。
units.en: Mo then sent Zhi as hostage to Shi Le, who distrusted Mo and forwarded his letter sealed to Liu Yao.
units.literal: Mo thereupon sent Zhi as hostage to Shi Le; Shi Le, because Mo was full of deceit, sealed Mo's letter and sent it to Liu Yao.

units.zh: 默使人伺得勒書，便突圍投李矩。
units.en: Mo's agents intercepted Shi Le's packet; he burst the siege and fled to Li Ju.
units.literal: Mo had men spy and obtain Shi Le's letter, then suddenly broke the encirclement and fled to Li Ju.

units.zh: 後與矩並力距劉、石，事見矩傳。
units.en: He later fought Liu Yao and the Shi alongside Li Ju, as told in Li Ju's biography.
units.literal: Later he jointly with Ju resisted Liu and Shi—the affair is seen in Ju's biography.

units.zh: 太興初，除潁川太守。
units.en: Early in Taixing he was named prefect of Yingchuan.
units.literal: At the beginning of Taixing, he was appointed prefect of Yingchuan.

units.zh: 默與石匆戰敗，矩轉蹙弱，默深憂懼，解印授其參軍殷嶠，謂之曰：「李使君遇吾甚厚，今遂棄去，無顏謝之，三日可白吾去也。」
units.en: Beaten by Shi Cong while Li Ju weakened, Guo Mo panicked, handed his seal to Yin Qiao, and said, "Li Ju has been generous; I cannot face him if I slip away—announce my flight in three days."
units.literal: Mo was defeated in battle with Shi Cong; Ju turned ever weaker; Mo was deeply worried and afraid; he handed his seal to his adjutant Yin Qiao, saying to him: "Prefect Li has treated me very generously; now I suddenly abandon him—I have no face to thank him; within three days you may report my departure."

units.zh: 乃奔陽翟。
units.en: He bolted for Yangzhai.
units.literal: Thereupon he fled to Yangzhai.

units.zh: 矩聞之，大怒，遣其將郭誦追默，至襄城，及之。
units.en: Li Ju, enraged, sent Guo Song after him and ran him down at Xiangcheng.
units.literal: When Ju heard it, he was greatly angry, sent his general Guo Song to pursue Mo, reached Xiangcheng, and overtook him.

units.zh: 默棄家人，單馬馳去。
units.en: Guo Mo abandoned his family and galloped off alone.
units.literal: Mo abandoned wife and children and alone on horseback galloped away.

units.zh: 默至京都，明帝授征虜將軍。
units.en: At the capital Emperor Ming named him General Who Punishes Captives.
units.literal: When Mo reached the capital district, Emperor Ming appointed him General Who Punishes Captives.

units.zh: 劉遐卒，以默為北中郎將、監淮北軍事、假節。
units.en: After Liu Xia died he became north camp general of the guard, supervisor of Huai defense, with baton of authority.
units.literal: When Liu Xia died, Mo was appointed north camp general of the guard, supervisor of military affairs north of the Huai, with credential.

units.zh: 遐故部曲李龍等謀反，詔默與右衛將軍趙胤討平之。
units.en: Liu Xia's old followers Li Long and others plotted revolt; the court ordered Guo Mo and Zhao Yin of the right guard to crush them.
units.literal: Xia's old retainers Li Long and others plotted rebellion; an edict ordered Mo and guard general of the right Zhao Yin jointly to punish and pacify them.

units.zh: 朝廷將征蘇峻，懼其為亂，召默拜後將軍，領屯騎校尉。
units.en: When the court moved against Su Jun it feared Guo Mo might stir trouble, so it summoned him as rear general and colonel of the camp cavalry.
units.literal: The court was about to campaign against Su Jun and feared he would cause chaos; it summoned Mo and appointed him rear general, concurrently colonel of the encampment cavalry.

units.zh: 初戰有功，及六軍敗績，南奔。
units.en: He fought well at first, but when the imperial host collapsed he ran south.
units.literal: In the first battle he had merit; when the six armies were routed, he fled south.

units.zh: 郗鑒議于曲阿北大業裏作壘，以分賊勢，使默守之。
units.en: Xi Jian proposed a fort north of Qu'a at Daye to split Su Jun's strength and put Guo Mo in charge of it.
units.literal: Xi Jian deliberated on building a fort north of Qu'a at Daye village to divide the bandits' force and had Mo defend it.

units.zh: 峻遣韓晁等攻默甚急，壘中頗乏水，默懼，分人馬出外，乃潛從南門蕩出，留人堅守。
units.en: Su Jun sent Han Chao to hammer the fort; water ran low and Guo Mo panicked—he slipped part of his force outside, then broke out the south gate under cover while leaving a rear guard.
units.literal: Su Jun sent Han Chao and others to attack Mo very urgently; inside the fort they were quite short of water; Mo feared, divided men and horses to go outside, then secretly slipped out from the south gate in a dash, leaving men to hold fast on defense.

units.zh: 會峻死，圍解，徵為右軍將軍。
units.en: When Su Jun died the ring broke, and Guo Mo was recalled as general of the right army.
units.literal: It happened that Su Jun died; the siege was lifted; Mo was summoned as general of the right army.

units.zh: 默樂為邊將，不願宿衛，及赴召，謂平南將軍劉胤曰：「我能禦胡而不見用。
units.en: Guo Mo preferred life on the border to palace duty. When the summons came he told General Who Pacifies the South, Liu Yin, "I can hold the steppe line yet the court will not use me.
units.literal: Mo delighted in being a frontier general and did not wish to serve in palace guard; when he went to answer the summons, he said to General Who Pacifies the South Liu Yin: "I can ward off the Hu yet am not employed.

units.zh: 右軍主禁兵，若疆場有虞，被使出征，方始配給，將卒無素，恩信不著，以此臨敵，少有不敗矣。
units.en: The general of the right leads the household guards: if the frontier flares, he is sent out on the spur of the moment, given troops he has never led—no bond of trust—and that is how he meets the enemy. Small wonder he almost always loses.
units.literal: The general of the right army commands the forbidden troops; if the borderlands have alarm, one is ordered out on campaign, and only then are troops assigned—officers and soldiers have no prior acquaintance, favor and trust are not established—with this to face the foe, scarcely one in few will not be defeated.

units.zh: 時當為官擇才，若人臣自擇官，安得不亂乎」胤曰：「所論事雖然，非小人所及也。」
units.en: The court should pick the man for the post, not the man the post. Let every officer choose his own job and the realm falls to ruin." Liu Yin answered, "You speak truth, but such things are above my station."
units.literal: The time ought to be that the office selects talent; if ministers themselves select office, how can there not be chaos?" Yin said: "The matters you discuss are indeed so, yet they are not what petty men can reach."

units.zh: 當發，求資於胤。
units.en: As he prepared to leave he hit Liu Yin for travel money.
units.literal: When he was about to depart, he sought funds from Yin.

units.zh: 時胤被詔免官，不即歸罪，方自申理，而驕侈更甚，遠近怪之。
units.en: Liu Yin had been dismissed but stayed on to plead his case, all the while living more arrogantly than ever; people talked from every quarter.
units.literal: At that time Yin had received an edict removing him from office but did not at once return to answer for guilt; he was justifying himself, yet arrogance and extravagance grew still worse; near and far marveled at it.

units.zh: 初，默之被征距蘇峻也，下次尋陽，見胤，胤參佐張滿等輕默，倮露視之，默常切齒。
units.en: When Guo Mo had first marched against Su Jun, he stopped at Xunyang and met Liu Yin; Zhang Man and other staffers sneered at him and made a public spectacle of his shame. Guo Mo never forgot it.
units.literal: Earlier, when Mo had been summoned to resist Su Jun, he next stopped at Xunyang, saw Yin; Yin's adjutants Zhang Man and others treated Mo lightly, exposed and humiliated him; Mo constantly ground his teeth.

units.zh: 至是，胤臘日餉默酒一器，肫一頭，默對信投之水中，忿憤益甚。
units.en: On the year-end la festival Liu Yin sent wine and a salted shank; Guo Mo had the courier watch as he flung the gifts into the river, his hatred sharper than ever.
units.literal: At this time, on the la day Yin presented Mo one vessel of wine and one head of pickled shank; Mo, facing the messenger, threw them into the water; rage and resentment grew still worse.

units.zh: 又僑人蓋肫先略取祖煥所殺孔煒女為妻，煒家求之，張滿等使還其家，肫不與，因與胤、滿有隙。
units.en: The refugee Gai Tun had earlier seized Kong Wei's daughter—Kong Wei murdered by Zu Huan—and made her his wife. Her kin demanded her back; Zhang Man forced Tun to release her, but Tun refused, which set him against Liu Yin and Zhang Man.
units.literal: Moreover the sojourner Gai Tun had earlier plundered and taken the daughter Kong Wei, whom Zu Huan had killed, as wife; Wei's family sought her; Zhang Man and others had her returned to her family; Tun would not give her, and therefore had a rift with Yin and Man.

units.zh: 至是，肫謂默曰：「劉江州不受免，密有異圖，與長史司馬張滿、荀楷等日夜計謀，反逆已形，惟忌郭侯一人，云當先除郭侯而後起事。
units.en: Then Tun told Guo Mo, "Liu Yin of Jiangzhou ignores his recall and plots treason with Zhang Man, Xun Kai, and the rest day and night. The thing is ripe; he only fears you, Lord Guo—word is he means to kill you first, then move.
units.literal: At this time Tun said to Mo: "Prefect Liu of Jiangzhou has not accepted dismissal and secretly harbors a different plan; with chief clerk Zhang Man, Xun Kai, and others he plots day and night; the shape of rebellion is already formed; he only fears Marquis Guo alone—they say he will first remove Marquis Guo and afterward raise the affair.

units.zh: 禍將至矣，宜深備之。」
units.en: Ruin is at hand; you must brace for it."
units.literal: Disaster is about to arrive; you should deeply prepare."

units.zh: 默既懷恨，便率其徒候旦門開襲胤。
units.en: Burning with old grudges, Guo Mo brought his men to the yamen gates at dawn and stormed Liu Yin.
units.literal: Mo, already harboring hatred, thereupon led his followers to wait until dawn when the gates opened and raided Yin.

units.zh: 胤將吏欲距默，默呴之曰：「我被詔有所討，動者誅及三族。」
units.en: Liu Yin's officers meant to fight; Guo Mo roared, "I carry an imperial warrant—anyone who moves will die with three degrees of kin."
units.literal: Yin's generals and clerks wished to resist Mo; Mo rebuked them, saying: "I have received an edict to punish someone; whoever moves will be executed to the third degree of kin."

units.zh: 遂入至內寢。
units.en: He pushed through to the private chambers.
units.literal: Thereupon he entered to the inner bedchamber.

units.zh: 胤尚與妾臥，默牽下斬之。
units.en: Liu Yin was still abed with a concubine; Guo Mo dragged him out and struck off his head.
units.literal: Yin was still lying with a concubine; Mo dragged him down and beheaded him.

units.zh: 出取胤僚佐張滿、荀楷等，誣以大逆。
units.en: He seized Zhang Man, Xun Kai, and the rest of Liu Yin's staff on trumped-up charges of treason.
units.literal: He went out and seized Yin's staff Zhang Man, Xun Kai, and others, falsely accusing them of great treason.

units.zh: 傳胤首于京師，詐作詔書，宜視內外。
units.en: He shipped Liu Yin's head to the capital, forged an edict, and had it read aloud inside and out.
units.literal: He sent Yin's head to the capital, forged an edict, and proclaimed it within and without.

units.zh: 掠胤女及諸妾，並金寶還船。
units.en: He looted Liu Yin's daughters, concubines, and treasure and withdrew to his fleet.
units.literal: He plundered Yin's daughters and concubines together with gold and jewels and returned to his boats.

units.zh: 初云下都，俄而還，停胤故府，招桓宣、王愆期。
units.en: He first announced a descent on the capital, then doubled back, occupied Liu Yin's old yamen, and called in Huan Xuan and Wang Yanqi.
units.literal: At first they said he would go down to the capital; soon he returned, stopped at Yin's old headquarters, and summoned Huan Xuan and Wang Yanqi.

units.zh: 愆期懼逼，勸默為平南、江州，默從之。
units.en: Wang Yanqi, afraid of being cornered, talked Guo Mo into claiming the titles General Who Pacifies the South and governor of Jiangzhou, and Mo agreed.
units.literal: Yanqi, fearing pressure, urged Mo to take the offices General Who Pacifies the South and Jiangzhou; Mo followed him.

units.zh: 愆期因逃廬山，桓宣固守不應。
units.en: Wang Yanqi bolted to Mount Lu while Huan Xuan shut his gates and refused the summons.
units.literal: Yanqi therefore fled to Mount Lu; Huan Xuan held fast and did not respond.

units.zh: 司徒王導懼不可制，乃大赦天下，梟胤首於大航，以默為西中郎將、豫州刺史。
units.en: Minister over the Masses Wang Dao, fearing he could not contain him, proclaimed a general amnesty, spiked Liu Yin's head on the Great Floating Bridge, and named Guo Mo west camp general of the guard and inspector of Yu province.
units.literal: Minister over the Masses Wang Dao, fearing he could not be controlled, thereupon proclaimed a general amnesty, displayed Yin's head on the Great Pontoon Bridge, and appointed Mo west camp general of the guard and inspector of Yu province.

units.zh: 武昌太守鄧岳馳白太尉陶侃，侃聞之，投袂起曰：「此必詐也。」
units.en: Deng Yue of Wuchang raced word to Tao Kan, who flung down his robe and cried, "This is a lie."
units.literal: Wuchang prefect Deng Yue galloped to report to grand commandant Tao Kan; when Kan heard it, he cast aside his sleeve and rose, saying: "This must be a fraud."

units.zh: 即日率眾討默，上疏陳默罪惡。
units.en: That very day he marched against Guo Mo and memorialized every crime.
units.literal: That same day he led the host to punish Mo and submitted a memorial stating Mo's crimes.

units.zh: 導聞之，乃收胤首，詔庾亮助侃討默。
units.en: Wang Dao, hearing this, recovered Liu Yin's head and ordered Yu Liang to join Tao Kan against Guo Mo.
units.literal: When Dao heard it, he thereupon took in Yin's head and ordered Yu Liang to aid Kan in punishing Mo.

units.zh: 默欲南據豫章，而侃已至城下築土山以臨之。
units.en: Guo Mo meant to slip south into Yuzhang, but Tao Kan was already below the walls throwing up siege mounds.
units.literal: Mo wished to hold Yuzhang to the south, but Kan had already arrived below the walls and built earthen hills overlooking them.

units.zh: 諸軍大集，圍之數重。
units.en: Imperial columns ringed him layer on layer.
units.literal: The various armies greatly gathered and besieged them in several layers.

units.zh: 侃惜默驍勇，欲活之，遣郭誦見默，默許降，而默將張醜、宋侯等恐為侃所殺，故致進退，不時得出。
units.en: Tao Kan admired Guo Mo's valor and meant to spare him; he sent Guo Song to treat for surrender. Guo Mo agreed, but Zhang Chou, Song Hou, and other officers feared Tao Kan would slaughter them, so they stalled and would not yield.
units.literal: Kan prized Mo's fierce courage and wished to keep him alive; he sent Guo Song to see Mo; Mo consented to surrender, but Mo's generals Zhang Chou, Song Hou, and others feared being killed by Kan, therefore caused hesitation in advancing and retreating and could not promptly come out.

units.zh: 攻之轉急，宋侯遂縛默求降，即斬於軍門，同黨死者四十人，傳首京師。
units.en: As the assault tightened, Song Hou bound Guo Mo and offered capitulation; Tao Kan had him beheaded at the camp gate along with forty accomplices, and sent the head to the capital.
units.literal: The attack grew more urgent; Song Hou thereupon bound Mo seeking surrender; he was immediately beheaded at the army gate; forty of the same faction died; the head was sent to the capital.

units.zh: 【史評】
units.en: Historian's appraisal
units.literal: Historian's appraisal

units.zh: 史臣曰：邵、李、魏、郭等諸將，契闊喪亂之辰，驅馳戎馬之際，威懷足以容眾，勇略足以制人，乃保據危城，折沖千里，招集義勇，抗禦仇讎，雖艱阻備嘗，皆乃心王室。
units.en: The chronicler writes: Through collapse and exile, Shao Xu, Li Ju, Wei Jun, Guo Mo, and their like rode the storm—humane enough to hold a following, bold enough to master events. They clung to doomed towns, blunted enemies a thousand li away, rallied loyal bands, and faced down hated foes. They tasted every hardship yet kept faith with the Jin.
units.literal: The historian says: The generals Shao, Li, Wei, Guo, and others, in the season of separation and ruin, galloping amid war-horses, had majesty and kindness enough to embrace the host, courage and strategy enough to control men; they protected and held perilous cities, repelled foes a thousand li, gathered righteous warriors, and resisted hated enemies; although hardships and obstructions were fully tasted, all bent their hearts to the royal house.

units.zh: 而矩能以少擊眾，戰勝獲多，遂使玄明憤恚，世龍挫衄。
units.en: Li Ju in particular beat larger hosts again and again, stinging Liu Cong into fury and bruising Shi Le.
units.literal: Yet Ju was able with few to strike many, winning battles and taking many captives, thereby causing Liu Cong, Xuanming, to rage with resentment and Shi Le, Shilong, to suffer defeat.

units.zh: 惜其寡弱，功虧一簣。
units.en: They were too few and too weak, and victory slipped from their grasp at the last.
units.literal: It is regrettable that they were few and weak and merit failed one basket short.

units.zh: 方之數子，其最優乎！
units.en: Set beside the others, Li Ju was the finest of them all.
units.literal: Compared to these several men, was he not the most excellent!

units.zh: 默既拔跡危亡，參陪朝伍，忿因眥睚，禍及誅夷，非夫狂悖，豈宜至此！
units.en: Guo Mo climbed from the wreckage into court, then murdered over a sidelong glance—only a man deranged beyond measure ends so.
units.literal: Mo, having pulled himself from danger and death and joined the court ranks, in resentment because of a sidelong glance brought disaster reaching execution and extermination—if he were not mad and perverse, how could it properly reach this!

units.zh: 段匹磾本自遐方，而系心朝廷，始則盡忠國難，終乃抗節虜廷，自蘇子卿以來，一人而已。
units.en: Duan Pidi was a man of the far steppe yet pinned his heart on the Jin: first he spent his loyalty in the dynasty's darkest hour, then died unbent in a barbarian court—since Su Wu there has been only one such man.
units.literal: Duan Pidi originally came from a distant region yet tied his heart to the court; at first he exhausted loyalty in the state's crisis, at the end upheld integrity in the barbarian court; since Su Ziqing, there has been only one man.

units.zh: 越石之見誅段氏，實以威名；
units.en: Liu Kun fell to the Duan blade chiefly because his fame terrified them;
units.literal: Yueshi's being executed by the Duan clan was truly because of awesome reputation;

units.zh: 匹磾之取戮世龍，亦由眾望：禍福之應，何其速哉！
units.en: Duan Pidi died at Shi Le's hands for the same reason—the expectations of the crowd. How swiftly blessing turns to bane!
units.literal: Pidi's receiving execution at Shilong's hands was likewise because of the host's hopes: how swift were the responses of fortune and disaster!

units.zh: 《詩》云：「無言不酬，無德不報」，此之謂也。
units.en: As the Classic of Poetry says, "No word spoken goes unanswered; no kindness shown goes unrepaid"—here is the proof.
units.literal: The Classic of Poetry says: "For no word is there no answer; for no virtue is there no recompense"—this is what it speaks of.

units.zh: 贊曰：邵李諸將，實惟忠壯。
units.en: The eulogy reads: Shao Xu and Li Ju were men of steadfast loyalty.
units.literal: The encomium says: The generals Shao and Li were truly loyal and stalwart.

units.zh: 蒙犯艱危，驅馳亭鄣。
units.en: They braved every danger and rode the border forts.
units.literal: They braved hardship and peril and galloped among frontier watchtowers.

units.zh: 力小任重，功虧身喪。
units.en: Their strength was slight for the weight they bore; their work unfinished, they perished.
units.literal: Their strength was small yet their burden heavy; merit failed and their persons perished.

units.zh: 匹磾勁烈，隕身全節。
units.en: Duan Pidi was iron to the core: he died but kept his honor whole.
units.literal: Pidi was fierce and upright; he lost his life yet preserved his integrity.

units.zh: 默實凶殘，自貽罪戾。
units.en: Guo Mo was savagery itself and reaped the ruin he sowed.
units.literal: Mo was truly fierce and cruel and brought guilt and crime on himself.
